title.en: Volume 435 Biographies 194: Confucian Scholars 5 - Fan Chong, Zhu Zhen, Hu Anguo and sons: Yin, Hong, Ning
title.raw: 卷四百三十五 列傳第一百九十四 儒林五 范沖 朱震 胡安國子:寅 宏 寧 Volume 435 Biographies 194: Confucian Scholars 5 - Fan Chong, Zhu Zhen, Hu Anguo and sons: Yin, Hong, Ning

sentences.zh: 范冲，字元長，登紹聖進士第。

translations.literal: Fan Chong, styled Yuanchang, passed the jinshi examination in the Shaosheng era.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chong, whose courtesy name was Yuanchang, obtained his jinshi degree in the Shaosheng reign period.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，召為虞部員外郎，俄出為兩淮轉運副使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, [Chong] was summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue; soon he was sent out as Vice Commissioner of Transport for the Two Huai circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong came to the throne, Chong was called to serve as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, and before long was posted as Vice Commissioner of Transport for the Two Huai circuits.

sentences.zh: 紹興中，隆祐皇后誕日，上置酒宮中，從容語及前朝事，後曰：「吾老矣，有所懷為官家言之。

translations.literal: In the Shaoxing era, on Empress Dowager Longyou's birthday, the Emperor set out wine in the palace and spoke at ease of affairs of the former dynasty. The Empress said: "I am old; I have something on my mind to tell you, Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaoxing period, on the birthday of Empress Dowager Longyou, the emperor held a banquet in the palace and spoke at leisure of matters from the previous reign. The empress said, "I am old now, and there is something I wish to say to you, Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 吾逮事宣仁聖烈皇后，聰明母儀，古今未見其比。

translations.literal: I once served Empress Dowager Xuanren the Sagely and Virtuous; her wisdom and maternal demeanor have never been matched in antiquity or the present.
translations.idiomatic: I once attended Empress Dowager Xuanren, the Sagely and Virtuous; in wisdom and dignity as a mother of the realm, none in past or present has ever equaled her.

sentences.zh: 曩因姦臣誣謗，有玷聖德，建炎初雖下詔辨明，而史錄未經刪定，無以傳信後世，而慰在天之靈也。

translations.literal: Formerly, because treacherous ministers slandered her, the sagely virtue was stained. Although at the beginning of Jianyan an edict clarified the matter, the historical record has not been revised and purged, so that it cannot transmit trust to posterity and comfort the spirit in Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago treacherous ministers defamed her and stained her sacred reputation. Although an edict at the start of the Jianyan era cleared her name, the historical record has never been edited and settled, so that truth cannot be handed down to later ages and her spirit in Heaven cannot be consoled.

sentences.zh: 」上悚然，亟詔重修神、哲兩朝《實錄》，召冲為宗正少卿兼直史館。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was startled and immediately decreed a thorough revision of the Veritable Records of the Shenzong and Zhezong reigns, summoning Chong as Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court with concurrent duty in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was deeply moved and at once ordered the Veritable Records of the Shenzong and Zhezong reigns to be thoroughly revised, summoning Chong to serve as Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court with concurrent appointment in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 冲父祖禹，元祐中嘗修《神宗實錄》，盡書王安石之過，以明神宗之聖。

translations.literal: Chong's father Zuyu, in the Yuanyou era, had once compiled the Veritable Record of Emperor Shenzong, fully recording Wang Anshi's faults to make clear Emperor Shenzong's sagacity.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's father Fan Zuyu had compiled the Veritable Record of Emperor Shenzong during the Yuanyou era, setting down all of Wang Anshi's errors so as to make plain the emperor's own sagacity.

sentences.zh: 其後安石婿蔡卞惡之，祖禹坐謫死嶺表。

translations.literal: Later Wang Anshi's son-in-law Cai Bian hated this; Zuyu was demoted on account of it and died in the Lingnan region.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Anshi's son-in-law Cai Bian took offense at this work, and Zuyu was banished on that account and died in the far south.

sentences.zh: 至是復以命冲，上謂之曰：「兩朝大典，皆為姦臣所壞，故以屬卿。

translations.literal: At this time the task was again entrusted to Chong. The Emperor told him: "The great compilations of both reigns were both ruined by treacherous ministers; therefore I entrust them to you."
translations.idiomatic: Now the commission was given again to Chong. The emperor said to him, "The great chronicles of both reigns were ruined by treacherous ministers; that is why I entrust this work to you."

sentences.zh: 」冲因論熙寧創置，元祐復古，紹聖以降弛張不一，本末先後，各有所因。

translations.literal: " Chong then discussed the institutions newly established in the Xining era, the restoration of antiquity in Yuanyou, and from the Shaosheng era onward the inconsistent tightening and loosening—root and branch, prior and subsequent, each had its causes.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong went on to discuss how the Xining reign had created new institutions, how Yuanyou had restored older ways, and how from Shaosheng onward policy had alternately tightened and relaxed—each change, he argued, had its own root causes in sequence and circumstance.

sentences.zh: 又極言王安石變法度之非，蔡京誤國之罪。

translations.literal: He also spoke at length on the wrongness of Wang Anshi's reform of laws and institutions, and Cai Jing's crime of misleading the state.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke at length against Wang Anshi's reforms of laws and institutions and against Cai Jing's crime of having misled the state.

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之，遷起居郎。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted this, and promoted him to Attendant Gentleman for Court Audiences.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his counsel and promoted him to Attendant Gentleman for Court Audiences.

sentences.zh: 俄開講筵，陞兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Soon the lecture hall was opened, and he was promoted to concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the imperial lecture hall was opened, and he was promoted to serve concurrently as Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 上雅好《左氏春秋》，命冲與朱震專講。

translations.literal: The Emperor was fond of the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and ordered Chong and Zhu Zhen to lecture on it exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was especially fond of the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and ordered Chong and Zhu Zhen to lecture on it exclusively.

sentences.zh: 冲敷衍經旨，因以規諷，上未嘗不稱善。

translations.literal: Chong elaborated the purport of the classic and thereby offered admonition; the Emperor never failed to praise it.
translations.idiomatic: Chong would unfold the meaning of the text and use it to offer gentle remonstrance, and the emperor never failed to commend him.

sentences.zh: 會皇子建國公瑗出就傅，首命冲以徽猷閣待制提舉建隆觀，為資善堂翊善，而朱震兼贊讀。

translations.literal: When the prince Guogong Yuan went out to receive instruction, Chong was first appointed Acting Commissioner of the Huiyou Pavilion, directing the Jianlong Abbey, as Adjutant Goodness for the Hall of Supporting Goodness, while Zhu Zhen served concurrently as Lecturer and Reader.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince, Guogong Yuan, left the palace to take up his studies, Chong was first appointed acting commissioner of the Huiyou Pavilion and director of the Jianlong Abbey, to serve as adjutant tutor in the Hall of Supporting Goodness, while Zhu Zhen served concurrently as lecturer and reader.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕為宗廟社稷大計，不敢私於一身，選於屬籍，得藝祖七世孫鞠之宮中。

translations.literal: The edict said: "We, for the great plan of the ancestral temple and state altars, dare not be partial to our own person; We selected from the imperial clansmen and obtained a seventh-generation descendant of Founder Taizu to rear in the palace."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "For the great design of the ancestral temple and the altars of state, We dare not indulge Our private person. Choosing from among the imperial clan, We found a seventh-generation descendant of our dynastic founder and reared him within the palace."

sentences.zh: 茲擇剛辰，出就外傅，宜有端良之士以充輔導之官，博觀在廷，無以易汝冲，德行文學，為時正人。

translations.literal: Now on this chosen auspicious day he goes out to receive an outer tutor; upright and excellent scholars should fill the offices of assistants and guides. Looking broadly at the court, none can replace you, Chong—in virtue and conduct and literary learning you are an upright man of the age."
translations.idiomatic: On this chosen auspicious day he goes forth to take an outer tutor. Upright and excellent men should fill the posts that guide and instruct him. Surveying the whole court, We find none to replace you, Chong: in conduct, virtue, and learning you are a man of integrity in this age."

sentences.zh: 乃祖發議嘉祐之初，乃父納忠元祐之際，敷求是似，尚有典刑。

translations.literal: Your grandfather raised proposals at the beginning of the Jiayou era; your father offered loyal counsel in the Yuanyou period. To spread and seek such likeness—there still remains the model of past worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Your grandfather advanced proposals at the opening of the Jiayou era; your father offered loyal counsel in the Yuanyou period. To spread such examples and seek their likeness is still to preserve the standards of former worthies.

sentences.zh: 顧資善之開，史館經筵，姑仍厥舊。

translations.literal: As for the opening of the Hall of Supporting Goodness, the Historiography Institute and the lecture hall—for the time being keep the old arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: As for the opening of the Hall of Supporting Goodness, the Historiography Institute, and the lecture hall, for the present let the former arrangements stand.

sentences.zh: 朕方求多聞之益，爾實兼數器之長，施及童蒙，綽有餘裕。

translations.literal: We are now seeking the benefit of much learning; you truly combine the strengths of many capacities. Applied to the young and ignorant, you will have ample surplus.
translations.idiomatic: We are now seeking the benefit of broad learning, and you truly unite many kinds of excellence. Applied to a child still in his first studies, you will have more than enough to spare.

sentences.zh: 蔽自朕志，宜即安之。

translations.literal: This proceeds from Our will; you should forthwith take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: This is Our settled wish; you should take up the post at once.

sentences.zh: 」時張浚在長沙，亦薦冲、震可備訓導。

translations.literal: " At the time Zhang Jun was at Changsha and also recommended Chong and Zhen as fit to serve in instruction.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Zhang Jun, stationed at Changsha, also recommended Chong and Zhen as fit to serve in the prince's instruction.

sentences.zh: 冲、震皆一時名德老成，極天下之選，上命建國公見翊善、贊讀，皆納拜。

translations.literal: Chong and Zhen were both eminent elders of virtue of the age, the utmost selection under Heaven. The Emperor ordered Prince Guogong to meet the Adjutant Goodness and Lecturer-Reader and all paid obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and Zhen were both eminent men of established virtue, the finest choice in the realm. The emperor ordered Prince Guogong to receive the adjutant tutor and lecturer-reader with full ceremonial obeisance.

sentences.zh: 俄遷翰林學士兼侍讀，冲力辭，改翰林侍讀學士，用其父故事也。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Hanlin Academician with concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting. Chong strenuously declined and was changed to Hanlin Lecturer-in-Waiting Academician, following his father's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Hanlin Academician with concurrent service as lecturer-in-waiting, but Chong firmly declined and was instead made Hanlin Lecturer-in-Waiting Academician, following his father's precedent.

sentences.zh: 尋以龍圖閣直學士奉祠。

translations.literal: Shortly he was made a recipient of sacrificial offerings as a direct academician of the Longtu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed a direct academician of the Longtu Hall with the privilege of receiving sacrificial emoluments.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 冲之修《神宗實錄》也，為《考異》一書，明示去取，舊文以墨書，刪去者以黃書，新修者以朱書，世號「朱墨史」。

translations.literal: When Chong revised the Veritable Record of Emperor Shenzong, he composed a book called Examination of Differences that clearly showed what was kept and discarded: old text in black ink, what was deleted in yellow, what was newly revised in red—the age called it "Red and Black History."
translations.idiomatic: In revising the Veritable Record of Emperor Shenzong, Chong compiled a work called Examination of Differences that made plain what was retained and what was removed: the old text in black, deletions in yellow, and new revisions in red. His contemporaries called it the "Red-and-Black History."

sentences.zh: 及修《哲宗實錄》，別為一書，名《辨誣錄》。

translations.literal: When he revised the Veritable Record of Emperor Zhezong, he separately made another book named Record of Refuting Slander.
translations.idiomatic: When he revised the Veritable Record of Emperor Zhezong, he produced a separate work entitled Record of Refuting Slander.

sentences.zh: 冲性好義樂善，司馬光家屬皆依冲所，冲撫育之。

translations.literal: Chong by nature loved righteousness and delighted in doing good; the family members of Sima Guang all relied on Chong's place, and Chong nurtured them.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Chong loved righteousness and delighted in doing good. The dependents of Sima Guang's household all looked to him, and he cared for them.

sentences.zh: 為光編類《記聞》十卷奏御，請以光之族曾孫宗召主光祀。

translations.literal: He compiled Guang's Record of What I Heard in ten juan for presentation to the throne, and requested that Guang's clansman's great-grandson Zongzhao preside over Guang's sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He edited Guang's Record of What I Heard into ten fascicles and presented them to the throne, asking that Guang's great-great-grandson Zongzhao be appointed to preside over Guang's sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 又嘗薦尹焞自代云。

translations.literal: He also once recommended Yin Chun to succeed him, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: It is also recorded that he once recommended Yin Chun to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 朱震，字子發，荊門軍人。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhen, styled Zifa, was a native of Jingmen Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhen, courtesy name Zifa, was a native of Jingmen.

sentences.zh: 登政和進士第，仕州縣以廉稱。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the Zhenghe era and served in prefectures and districts, known for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the Zhenghe era and served in local government, where he was known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 胡安國一見大器之，薦於高宗，召為司勳員外郎，震稱疾不至。

translations.literal: Hu Anguo upon one meeting regarded him as great talent and recommended him to Emperor Gaozong, who summoned him as Vice Director of the Ministry of Merits—but Zhen pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Anguo, upon meeting him once, recognized his great promise and recommended him to Emperor Gaozong, who summoned him to the post of Vice Director of the Ministry of Merits; Zhen pleaded illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 會江西制置使趙鼎入為參知政事，上諮以當世人才，鼎曰：「臣所知朱震，學術深博，廉正守道，士之冠冕，使位講讀，必有益於陛下。

translations.literal: When Jiangxi Circuit Military Commissioner Zhao Ding entered the capital as Vice Grand Councillor, the Emperor consulted him on the talents of the age. Ding said: "The Zhu Zhen I know—learning profound and broad, integrity upright and holding to the Way—is the cap of scholars. If placed in lecturing and reading, he will certainly benefit Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Ding, military commissioner of Jiangxi, entered the capital as vice grand councilor, the emperor asked him about the leading men of the day. Ding said, "The Zhu Zhen I know has learning both deep and broad, is upright and steadfast in the Way, and stands at the head of scholars. If he were placed among those who lecture and read to Your Majesty, he would surely be of benefit."

sentences.zh: 」上乃召之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then summoned him.

sentences.zh: 既至，上問以《易》、《春秋》之旨，震具以所學對。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the Emperor asked him about the purport of the Changes and Spring and Autumn; Zhen fully answered according to his learning.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, the emperor questioned him on the meaning of the Book of Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals, and Zhen answered fully from his own learning.

sentences.zh: 上說，擢為祠部員外郎，兼川、陝、荊、襄都督府詳議官。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and promoted him to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, with concurrent duty as Review Officer for the Shaanxi-Sichuan-Hubei Military Command headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and promoted him to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, with concurrent appointment as review officer on the staff of the military headquarters for Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, and Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 震因言：「荊、襄之間，沿漢上下，膏腴之田七百餘里，若選良將領部曲鎮之，招集流亡，務農種穀，寇來則禦，寇去則耕，不過三年，兵食自足。

translations.literal: Zhen therefore said: "Between Jing and Xiang, along the Han River upstream and downstream, are more than seven hundred li of fertile fields. If a good general is selected to garrison troops there, gathering fugitive populations, devoting effort to farming and planting grain—when bandits come, defend; when they leave, cultivate—within no more than three years, provisions for troops will be self-sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen then said, "Between Jingzhou and Xiangyang, along the upper and lower reaches of the Han, lie more than seven hundred li of rich farmland. If a capable general were chosen to station troops there, gather the displaced, and devote them to farming and grain planting—fighting when the enemy comes, plowing when they withdraw—within three years the army's food supply would be secure."

sentences.zh: 又給茶鹽鈔於軍中，募人中糴，可以下江西之舟，通湘中之粟。

translations.literal: " Moreover, issue tea-salt notes to the army and recruit people within to purchase grain; this can unload boats from Jiangxi and connect grain from central Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: " Moreover, if tea-and-salt exchange notes were issued to the army and men were recruited to buy grain on the spot, boats from Jiangxi could be relieved of their burden and grain from central Hunan could be brought through."

sentences.zh: 觀釁而動，席卷河南，此以逸待勞，萬全計也。」

translations.literal: " Watch for openings and act; sweep across Henan—this is to await the weary with the rested, a plan of ten thousand assurances."
translations.idiomatic: " Watch for the moment to strike and sweep across the North China plain—this is to meet a weary foe with rested troops, a plan of complete security."

sentences.zh: 遷秘書少監兼侍經筵，轉起居郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat with concurrent duty at the classic lecture, then to Attendant Gentleman for Court Audiences.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat with concurrent service at the classic lecture, and then transferred to Attendant Gentleman for Court Audiences.

sentences.zh: 建國公出就傅，以震為讚讀，仍賜五品服。

translations.literal: When Prince Guogong went out to receive instruction, Zhen was made Lecturer-Reader and still granted fifth-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Guogong left the palace to take up his studies, Zhen was appointed lecturer-reader and was also granted robes of the fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人兼翊善。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat with concurrent Adjutant Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat with concurrent appointment as adjutant tutor.

sentences.zh: 時郭千里除將作監丞，震言：「千里侵奪民田，曾經按治，願寢新命。

translations.literal: At the time Guo Qianli was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings. Zhen said: "Qianli seized and encroached on people's fields; he has already been investigated and punished. We ask that the new appointment be suspended."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Guo Qianli was appointed vice director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings. Zhen said, "Qianli seized and encroached upon the people's fields and has already been investigated and punished. I ask that this new appointment be withdrawn."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " [The Emperor] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 轉給事中兼直學士院，遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervisory Attendant of the Secretariat with concurrent duty in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, then to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Supervisory Attendant of the Secretariat with concurrent service in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and then promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 是時，虔州民為盜，天子以為憂，選良太守往慰撫之。

translations.literal: At that time the people of Qian Prefecture became bandits; the Son of Heaven was troubled and selected a good prefect to go comfort and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the people of Qianzhou had turned to banditry, and the emperor, deeply troubled, chose a capable prefect to go and reassure them.

sentences.zh: 將行，震曰：「使居官者廉而不擾，則百姓自安，雖誘之為盜，亦不為矣。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, Zhen said: "If those in office are incorrupt and do not harass, then the common people will of themselves be at peace—even if tempted to become bandits, they will not do so."
translations.idiomatic: As the prefect was about to depart, Zhen said, "If those who hold office are honest and do not harass the people, the common folk will settle down of themselves; even if someone tried to lure them into banditry, they would not go."

sentences.zh: 願詔新太守到官之日，條具本郡及屬縣官吏有貪墨無狀者，一切罷去，聽其自擇慈祥仁惠之人，有治效者優加獎勸。

translations.literal: " We ask that an edict be issued that when the new prefect arrives, he shall itemize all corrupt and baseless officials of this prefecture and its subordinate counties and dismiss them all, allowing him to select on his own kindly and benevolent persons; those with governance achievements should be specially rewarded and encouraged."
translations.idiomatic: " I ask that an edict be issued requiring the new prefect, on the day he takes office, to list every corrupt and unworthy official in the prefecture and its subordinate counties and dismiss them all, while allowing him to choose on his own men who are kindly and benevolent, and to reward those who govern well."

sentences.zh: 」上從其言。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 故事，當喪無享廟之禮。

translations.literal: By precedent, during mourning there was no rite of enjoying the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: By established precedent, while mourning was in force there was no rite of offering sacrifice at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 時徽宗未祔廟，太常少卿吳表臣奏行明堂之祭。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Huizong had not yet been enshrined; Vice Director of Sacrificial Rites Wu Biaochen memorialized to hold the Bright Hall sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Huizong had not yet been enshrined in the ancestral temple, and Vice Director of Sacrificial Rites Wu Biaochen memorialized that the Bright Hall sacrifice should be performed.

sentences.zh: 震因言：「《王制》：『喪三年不祭，惟天地社稷為越紼而行事。

translations.literal: Zhen therefore said: "The Royal Regulations: 'During three years of mourning there is no sacrifice, except that for Heaven-and-Earth and the soil-grain altars one may act with the mourning cord pulled aside over the arm.'"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen then said, "The Royal Regulations states, 'During the three years of mourning no sacrifices are performed, except that for Heaven and Earth and for the altars of soil and grain one may carry out the rites with the mourning sash drawn aside over the arm.'"

sentences.zh: 』《春秋》書『夏五月乙酉，吉，禘於莊公』，《公羊傳》曰：『譏始不三年也。

translations.literal: " The Spring and Autumn records: 'In summer, fifth month, day yiyou—auspicious—li sacrifice at the temple of Duke Zhuang.' The Gongyang Commentary says: 'It criticizes that at the outset the three-year mourning was not observed.'"
translations.idiomatic: " The Spring and Autumn Annals records, 'In summer, the fifth month, on the day yiyou, an auspicious day, a li sacrifice was performed for Duke Zhuang.' The Gongyang Commentary explains this as a rebuke because the three-year mourning had not been observed from the beginning."

sentences.zh: 』國朝景德二年，真宗居明德皇后喪，既易月而除服，明年遂享太廟，合祀天地於圜丘。

translations.literal: " In our dynasty in the second year of Jingde, when Emperor Zhenzong was in mourning for Empress Mingde, after the month was changed the mourning garments were removed; the next year he enjoyed the Grand Temple and combined sacrifice of Heaven and Earth at the Round Mound."
translations.idiomatic: " In our own dynasty, in the second year of the Jingde era, when Emperor Zhenzong was in mourning for Empress Mingde, he changed the mourning month and then laid aside his mourning garments; the following year he offered sacrifice at the Grand Temple and joined Heaven and Earth in worship at the Round Mound."

sentences.zh: 當時未行三年之喪，專行以日易月之制可也，在今日行之則非也。

translations.literal: At that time the three-year mourning was not carried out; specially practicing the system of substituting days for months was acceptable—but to practice it today would be wrong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the full three-year mourning was not observed, and it was acceptable to follow only the practice of substituting days for months; to do the same today would be wrong.

sentences.zh: 」詔侍從、台諫、禮官參議，卒用御史趙渙、禮部侍郎陳公輔言，大饗明堂。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered attendant officials, remonstrance and review officials, and ritual officials to deliberate jointly; in the end they followed Supervisory Censor Zhao Huan and Vice Minister of Rites Chen Gongfu and greatly feasted at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered the attendant officials, the remonstrance and review offices, and the ritual officials to deliberate together; in the end the court followed the views of Supervisory Censor Zhao Huan and Vice Minister of Rites Chen Gongfu and held the great Bright Hall feast.

sentences.zh: 七年，震謝病丐祠，旋知禮部貢舉，會疾卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Zhen resigned on grounds of illness requesting sacrificial appointment; soon he oversaw the Ministry of Rites metropolitan examination, but before long he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Zhen resigned on grounds of illness and asked for a sacrificial appointment; he was soon put in charge of the metropolitan examination of the Ministry of Rites, but before long he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 震經學深醇，有《漢上易解》云：「陳摶以《先天圖》傳種放，放傳穆修，穆修傳李之才，之才傳邵雍。

translations.literal: Zhen's classical learning was profound and pure. In his Han River Commentary on the Changes he said: "Chen Tuan transmitted the Prior Heaven Diagram to Zhong Fang; Fang to Mu Xiu; Mu Xiu to Li Zhicai; Zhicai to Shao Yong."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's classical learning was profound and mature. In his Han River Commentary on the Changes he wrote, "Chen Tuan transmitted the Prior Heaven Diagram to Zhong Fang; Zhong Fang to Mu Xiu; Mu Xiu to Li Zhicai; and Li Zhicai to Shao Yong."

sentences.zh: 放以《河圖》、《洛書》傳李溉，溉傳許堅，許堅傳範諤昌，諤昌傳劉牧。

translations.literal: " Fang transmitted the Yellow River Diagram and Luo River Writing to Li Gai; Gai to Xu Jian; Jian to Fan Echang; Echang to Liu Mu."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhong Fang transmitted the Yellow River Diagram and the Luo River Writing to Li Gai; Li Gai to Xu Jian; Xu Jian to Fan Echang; and Fan Echang to Liu Mu."

sentences.zh: 穆修以《太極圖》傳周惇頤，惇頤傳程顥、程頤。

translations.literal: " Mu Xiu transmitted the Supreme Polarity Diagram to Zhou Dunyi; Dunyi to Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi."
translations.idiomatic: " Mu Xiu transmitted the Diagram of the Supreme Polarity to Zhou Dunyi; Zhou Dunyi to the Cheng brothers, Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi."

sentences.zh: 是時，張載講學於二程、邵雍之間。

translations.literal: " At that time Zhang Zai lectured between the two Chengs and Shao Yong."
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Zhang Zai taught and studied in the circle of the two Chengs and Shao Yong."

sentences.zh: 故雍著《皇極經世書》，牧陳天地五十有五之數，惇頤作《通書》，程頤著《易傳》，載造《太和》、《參兩》篇。

translations.literal: " Therefore Yong wrote the Book of the Royal Extreme through the Ages; Mu expounded the number fifty-five of Heaven and Earth; Dunyi wrote the Tongshu; Cheng Yi wrote the Commentary on the Changes; Zai composed the 'Grand Harmony' and 'Participating in the Two' chapters."
translations.idiomatic: " Thus Shao Yong wrote the Book of the Royal Extreme through the Ages; Liu Mu set forth the doctrine that Heaven and Earth number fifty-five; Zhou Dunyi wrote the Tongshu; Cheng Yi wrote the Commentary on the Changes; and Zhang Zai composed the chapters 'Grand Harmony' and 'Participating in the Two.'"

sentences.zh: 臣今以《易傳》為宗，和會雍、載之論，上采漢、魏、吳、晉，下逮有唐及今，包括異同，庶幾道離而復合。

translations.literal: " Your servant now takes Cheng Yi's Commentary as the core, harmonizing the discussions of Yong and Zai, ascending to gather Han, Wei, Wu, and Jin, descending to Tang and the present, including differences and similarities—perhaps the Way, though departed, may reunite."
translations.idiomatic: " I now take the Commentary on the Changes of Cheng Yi as my foundation, reconcile it with the doctrines of Shao Yong and Zhang Zai, draw upward from Han, Wei, Wu, and Jin, and extend downward through Tang to the present, embracing both agreements and differences, so that the Way, though scattered, may come together again."

sentences.zh: 」蓋其學以王弼盡去舊說，雜以莊、老，專尚文辭為非是，故其於象數加詳焉。

translations.literal: " In general his learning held that Wang Bi, by entirely discarding old explanations and mixing in Zhuangzi and Laozi while exclusively honoring literary phrasing, was in error; therefore he gave extra detail to image and number."
translations.idiomatic: " In general he held that Wang Bi was wrong to discard the older interpretations entirely, mix in Zhuangzi and Laozi, and prize literary elegance above all; for that reason he gave particular attention to images and numbers."

sentences.zh: 其論《圖》、《書》授受源委如此，蓋莫知其所自云。

translations.literal: His account of how the Diagrams and Writings were transmitted and received was thus—but probably no one knows from where they originated.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his account of how the Diagrams and Writings were handed down; yet in the end no one truly knows where they came from.

sentences.zh: 胡安國

translations.literal: Hu Anguo
translations.idiomatic: Hu Anguo

sentences.zh: 胡安國，字康侯，建寧崇安人。

translations.literal: Hu Anguo, styled Kanghou, was a native of Chong'an in Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Anguo, whose courtesy name was Kanghou, was a native of Chong'an in Jianning.

sentences.zh: 入太學，以程頤之友朱長文及潁川靳裁之為師。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial University, taking as teachers Zhu Changwen, friend of Cheng Yi, and Jin Caizhi of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial University and took as his teachers Zhu Changwen, a friend of Cheng Yi, and Jin Caizhi of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 裁之與論經史大義，深奇重之。

translations.literal: Caizhi in discussing the great principles of the classics and history deeply marveled at and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Caizhi discussed with him the great principles of the classics and history, he came to admire him deeply.

sentences.zh: 三試於禮部，中紹聖四年進士第。

translations.literal: He tested three times at the Ministry of Rites and passed the jinshi in the fourth year of Shaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: After three attempts at the Ministry of Rites examinations, he passed the jinshi in the fourth year of the Shaosheng era.

sentences.zh: 初，廷試考官定其策第一，宰職以無詆元祐語，遂以何昌言冠，方天若次之，又欲以宰相章惇子次天若。

translations.literal: Initially at the palace examination the examiners ranked his policy discourse first, but the chief ministers, because it contained no denunciation of Yuanyou language, placed He Changyan first, Fang Tianruo second, and further wished to place the son of Chief Councillor Zhang Dun third after Tianruo.
translations.idiomatic: At first the examiners for the palace examination ranked his policy essay first, but the chief ministers, because it contained no language attacking the Yuanyou faction, placed He Changyan first and Fang Tianruo second, and even wished to rank the son of Chief Councillor Zhang Dun just below Tianruo.

sentences.zh: 時發策大要崇復熙寧、元豐之制，安國推明《大學》，以漸復三代為對。

translations.literal: The questions issued that year broadly upheld restoring Xining and Yuanfeng institutions; Anguo in his answer developed the Great Learning, taking gradual restoration of the Three Dynasties as his reply.
translations.idiomatic: The examination questions that year broadly favored restoring the institutions of the Xining and Yuanfeng eras; Anguo, in his answer, developed the Great Learning and argued for a gradual return to the ways of the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 哲宗命再讀之，注聽稱善者數四，親擢為第三。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong ordered it read again; noting several places of praise, he personally elevated Anguo to third place.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong ordered the essay read again, listened closely, and praised it several times, then personally raised Anguo to third place.

sentences.zh: 為太學博士，足不躡權門。

translations.literal: He became a Erudite of the Imperial University and would not set foot in powerful houses.
translations.idiomatic: He became an erudite of the Imperial University and would not set foot in the houses of the powerful.

sentences.zh: 提舉湖南學事，有詔舉遺逸，安國以永州布衣王繪、鄧璋應詔。

translations.literal: As promoter of Hunan educational affairs, there was an edict to recommend recluses of outstanding talent; Anguo recommended the Yongzhou commoners Wang Hui and Deng Zhang to answer the edict.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as promoter of educational affairs in Hunan, he responded to an edict calling for the recommendation of recluses of outstanding talent by nominating the Yongzhou commoners Wang Hui and Deng Zhang.

sentences.zh: 二人老不行，安國請命之官，以勸為學者。

translations.literal: The two men were old and would not go; Anguo requested that they be ordered to offices, to encourage those who study.
translations.idiomatic: The two men were old and declined to take office, but Anguo asked that they nevertheless be granted official posts so as to encourage others in learning.

sentences.zh: 零陵簿稱二人黨人范純仁客，而流人鄒浩所請托也。

translations.literal: A clerk of Lingling claimed the two were associates of Yuanyou faction member Fan Chunren's guests, and that exiled man Zou Hao had requested the nomination.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk of Lingling claimed that the two men were clients of Fan Chunren of the Yuanyou faction and that the nomination had been arranged at the request of the exiled scholar Zou Hao.

sentences.zh: 蔡京素惡安國與己異，得簿言，大喜，命湖南提刑置獄推治，又移湖北再鞫，卒無驗，安國竟除名。

translations.literal: Cai Jing had long hated Anguo for differing from himself; obtaining the clerk's words he was greatly pleased and ordered the Hunan judicial intendant to set up a case and investigate; it was transferred to Hubei for re-examination—ultimately nothing was verified, but Anguo was still dismissed from his name.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing had long resented Anguo for standing apart from him; when he obtained the clerk's accusation he was delighted and ordered the Hunan judicial intendant to open a case and investigate. The inquiry was transferred to Hubei and heard again, but though nothing was proved, Anguo was nevertheless stripped of his office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，簿以他罪抵法，台臣直前事，復安國元官。

translations.literal: Before long the clerk was punished by law for another crime; censorial officials spoke up on the former affair and Anguo's original office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the clerk was punished for another offense, and the censorial officials spoke up about the earlier affair, whereupon Anguo's former office was restored.

sentences.zh: 政和元年，張商英相，除提舉成都學事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenghe, when Zhang Shangying was chief councillor, [Anguo] was appointed promoter of Chengdu educational affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhenghe era, when Zhang Shangying became chief councilor, Anguo was appointed promoter of educational affairs in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 二年，丁內艱，移江東。

translations.literal: In the second year he mourned his mother and was transferred to Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he entered mourning for his mother and was transferred to Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 父沒終喪，謂子弟曰：「吾昔為親而仕，今雖有祿萬鍾，將何所施？

translations.literal: When his father died and mourning ended, he told his sons and younger brothers: "Formerly I took office for my parents' sake; now though I have salary of ten thousand zhong, to whom shall I apply it?"
translations.idiomatic: When his father died and the mourning period had ended, he said to his sons and younger brothers, "In the past I took office for the sake of my parents; now, though I have an income of ten thousand zhong, to whom should I devote it?"

sentences.zh: 」遂稱疾不仕，築室墓傍，耕種取給，蓋將終身焉。

translations.literal: " He then pleaded illness and refused office, built a room beside the tomb, farmed for his subsistence, intending to end his days thus.
translations.idiomatic: " He then pleaded illness and refused office, built a dwelling beside the tomb, and supported himself by farming, intending to live out his life in that way.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，李彌大、吳敏、譚世勣合薦，除屯田郎，辭。

translations.literal: Near the end of Xuanhe, Li Mida, Wu Min, and Tan Shixun jointly recommended him; he was appointed Master of Dotted Fields but declined.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Xuanhe era, Li Mida, Wu Min, and Tan Shixun jointly recommended him; he was appointed Master of Dotted Fields but declined the post.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，除太常少卿，辭；

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang he was appointed Vice Director of Sacrificial Rites and declined;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jingkang era he was appointed Vice Director of Sacrificial Rites and declined;

sentences.zh: 除起居郎，又辭。

translations.literal: he was appointed Attendant Gentleman for Court Audiences, and again declined.
translations.idiomatic: he was appointed Attendant Gentleman for Court Audiences, and again declined.

sentences.zh: 朝旨屢趣行，至京師，以疾在告。

translations.literal: Court orders repeatedly urged him to proceed; he reached the capital and was on sick leave.
translations.idiomatic: Court orders repeatedly urged him to take up his post; he reached the capital but remained on sick leave.

sentences.zh: 一日方午，欽宗亟召見，安國奏曰：「明君以務學為急，聖學以正心為要。

translations.literal: One day at noon Emperor Qinzong urgently summoned an audience; Anguo memorialized: "An enlightened ruler makes pressing effort on learning; sagely learning takes rectifying the mind as the essential."
translations.idiomatic: One day at noon Emperor Qinzong urgently summoned him to audience. Anguo memorialized, "An enlightened ruler makes the pursuit of learning his first urgency; sagely learning takes the rectification of the mind as its foundation."

sentences.zh: 心者萬事之宗，正心者揆事宰物之權。

translations.literal: " The mind is the lord of the myriad affairs; rectifying the mind is the power to measure affairs and master things."
translations.idiomatic: " The mind is the source of the myriad affairs; to rectify the mind is to hold the authority by which affairs are judged and things are governed."

sentences.zh: 願擢名儒明於治國平天下之本者，虛懷訪問，深發獨智。

translations.literal: " We wish to select renowned Confucians clear on the root of governing the state and bringing peace under Heaven, visit them with empty mind, and deeply draw forth singular wisdom."
translations.idiomatic: " I ask that renowned scholars who understand the foundations of governing the state and bringing peace to the realm be elevated, consulted with an open mind, and allowed to bring forth their deepest insight."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「為天下國家必有一定不可易之計，謀議既定，君臣固守，故有志必成，治功可立。

translations.literal: " He also said: "To have a state under Heaven there must be a fixed plan that cannot be easily changed. Once deliberation is settled, ruler and ministers firmly hold to it—thus there is will to accomplish and governance achievements can be established."
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "To govern the realm there must be a settled plan that cannot lightly be altered. Once counsel has been decided, ruler and ministers must hold firmly to it; only then can purpose be fulfilled and good governance be achieved."

sentences.zh: 今南向視朝半年矣，而紀綱尚紊，風俗益衰，施置乖方，舉動煩擾。

translations.literal: " Now facing south to hold court for half a year already, yet regulations are still disorderly, customs daily decline, arrangements are misaligned, actions are vexingly troubled."
translations.idiomatic: " Your Majesty has faced south and held court for half a year already, yet discipline remains disorderly, customs grow daily worse, measures are ill chosen, and every action is vexatious and confused."

sentences.zh: 大臣爭競，而朋黨之患萌；

translations.literal: " Great ministers contend competitively and the affliction of factions arises;"
translations.idiomatic: " Great ministers contend with one another, and the scourge of faction begins to appear;"

sentences.zh: 百執窺覦，而浸潤之奸作。

translations.literal: " the hundred offices peep and covet, and creeping corruption takes form;"
translations.idiomatic: " the hundred offices watch and covet, and insidious wrongdoing takes shape;"

sentences.zh: 用人失當，而名器愈輕；

translations.literal: " employment of men is improper and honorific titles grow lighter;"
translations.idiomatic: " men are appointed improperly, and offices of honor are cheapened;"

sentences.zh: 出令數更，而士民不信。

translations.literal: " orders issued are frequently changed and scholars and common people do not trust."
translations.idiomatic: " edicts are issued and changed again and again, and neither scholars nor common people place any trust in the government."

sentences.zh: 若不掃除舊跡，乘勢更張，竊恐大勢一傾，不可復正。

translations.literal: " If we do not sweep away old traces and take advantage of momentum to renew completely, I fear the great momentum will once lean and cannot be righted again."
translations.idiomatic: " If the old abuses are not swept away and policy is not boldly renewed while there is still momentum to do so, I fear that once the great balance of the state tilts, it will never be set right again."

sentences.zh: 乞訪大臣，各令展盡底蘊，畫一具進。

translations.literal: I ask that great ministers be consulted and each be made to set forth his full knowledge, drawing up a unified plan for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the great ministers be consulted and that each be required to set forth his full understanding, drawing up a single unified plan for presentation.

sentences.zh: 先宣示台諫，使隨事疏駁。

translations.literal: First announce this to the remonstrance and review offices, so that they may memorialize objections on particular points as events arise.
translations.idiomatic: First announce this to the remonstrance and review offices, so that they may submit objections on particular points as matters arise.

sentences.zh: 若大臣議絀，則參用台諫之言；

translations.literal: If the great ministers' deliberations are deficient, then incorporate the views of the censorial remonstrators;
translations.idiomatic: If the great ministers' deliberations are deficient, then the views of the censorial remonstrators should be adopted;

sentences.zh: 若疏駁不當，則專守大臣之策。

translations.literal: if the objections are improper, then adhere solely to the great ministers' plans.
translations.idiomatic: if the objections are improper, then the court should adhere solely to the great ministers' plans.

sentences.zh: 仍集議於朝，斷自宸衷，按為國論，以次施行。

translations.literal: Still gather deliberation at court, let the imperial heart decide, fix this as national policy, and implement it step by step.
translations.idiomatic: The court should still gather for joint deliberation, let the imperial heart decide, fix this as national policy, and carry it out in order.

sentences.zh: 敢有動搖，必罰無赦。

translations.literal: Whoever dares to shake this [policy] will certainly be punished without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever dares to undermine this policy will certainly be punished without pardon.

sentences.zh: 庶幾新政有經，可冀中興。

translations.literal: Thus the new policies may have a constant thread, and restoration may be hoped for.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the new policies may have a constant thread, and restoration may be hoped for.

sentences.zh: 」欽宗曰：「比留詞掖相待，已命召卿試矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong said: "We have kept you in the drafting office waiting; We have already ordered to summon you for examination."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong said, "We have kept you in the drafting office awaiting your service, and have already ordered you summoned for examination."

sentences.zh: 」語未竟，日昃暑甚，汗洽上衣，遂退。

translations.literal: Before his words were finished, the sun was declining and the heat intense; sweat soaked his upper garment, and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had finished speaking, the sun was declining and the heat was intense; sweat soaked through his upper garment, and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時門下侍郎耿南仲倚攀附恩，凡與己不合者，即指為朋黨。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director of the Secretariat Geng Nanzhong relied on attached favor; whoever disagreed with him he labeled a faction member.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Vice Director of the Secretariat Geng Nanzhong relied on favor he had curried; whoever disagreed with him he labeled a factionalist.

sentences.zh: 見安國論奏，慍曰：「中興如此，而曰績效未見，是謗聖德也。

translations.literal: Seeing Anguo's memorial, he said angrily: "Restoration is thus, and yet he says results are not yet seen—this slanders the sacred virtue."
translations.idiomatic: When he saw Anguo's memorial, he said angrily, "Restoration is already under way, and yet he says that results are not yet seen—this is to slander the sacred virtue of the throne."

sentences.zh: 」乃言安國意窺經筵，不宜召試。

translations.literal: He then said Anguo's intent was to peer at the lecture seat and that he was unfit to be summoned for examination.
translations.idiomatic: He then said that Anguo's intent was to covet a place at the lecture seat and that he was unfit to be summoned for examination.

sentences.zh: 欽宗不答。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong did not reply.

sentences.zh: 安國屢辭，南仲又言安國不臣。

translations.literal: Anguo repeatedly declined; Nanzhong again said Anguo was disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo repeatedly declined office; Nanzhong again said that Anguo was disloyal.

sentences.zh: 欽宗問其狀，南仲曰：「往不事上皇，今又不事陛下。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong asked the particulars; Nanzhong said: "Formerly he would not serve the Retired Emperor; now he will not serve Your Majesty either."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong asked what he meant; Nanzhong said, "Formerly he would not serve the Retired Emperor; now he will not serve Your Majesty either."

sentences.zh: 」欽宗曰：「渠自以病辭，初非有向背也。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong said: "He himself pleads illness; at the outset there was no taking sides."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong said, "He himself pleads illness; from the first there was no question of taking sides."

sentences.zh: 」每臣僚登對，欽宗即問識胡安國否，中丞許翰曰：「自蔡京得政，士大夫無不受其籠絡，超然遠跡不為所汙如安國者實鮮。

translations.literal: Whenever ministers faced the throne, Emperor Qinzong would ask whether they knew Hu Anguo. Supervisory Censor Xu Han said: "Since Cai Jing held power, no scholar-official was not ensnared by him; those who kept aloof and left no trace of defilement like Anguo are truly few."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a minister faced the throne, Emperor Qinzong would ask whether he knew Hu Anguo. Supervisory Censor Xu Han said, "Since Cai Jing held power, no scholar-official was untouched by his nets; those who kept aloof and left no stain upon themselves, like Anguo, are truly few."

sentences.zh: 」欽宗歎息，遣中書舍人晁說之宣旨，令勉受命，且曰：「他日欲去，即不強留。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong sighed and sent Drafting Attendant Chao Shuozhi to proclaim the imperial will, bidding him accept office with effort, and said: "If you wish to leave another day, We will not strongly detain you."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong sighed and sent Drafting Attendant Chao Shuozhi to proclaim the imperial will, urging him to accept office, and said, "If you wish to leave on another day, We will not strongly detain you."

sentences.zh: 」既試，除中書舍人，賜三品服。

translations.literal: After the examination he was appointed Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and granted third-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: After the examination he was appointed Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat and granted robes of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 南仲諷台諫論其稽命不恭，宜從黜削。

translations.literal: Nanzhong incited the censorial remonstrators to say that his delay in obeying orders was disrespectful and he should be demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhong incited the censorial remonstrators to say that Anguo's delay in obeying orders was disrespectful and that he should be demoted.

sentences.zh: 疏奏不下，安國乃就職。

translations.literal: The memorial was not issued; Anguo then took up his post.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was not issued, and Anguo then took up his post.

sentences.zh: 南仲既傾宰相吳敏、樞密使李綱，又謂許景衡、晁說之視大臣升黜為去就，懷奸徇私，並黜之。

translations.literal: Nanzhong having already overthrown Chief Councillor Wu Min and Military Affairs Commissioner Li Gang, also said Xu Jingheng and Chao Shuozhi viewed great ministers' promotions and demotions as grounds for staying or leaving, harboring treachery and favoring private ties—both were dismissed together.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhong, having already overthrown Chief Councillor Wu Min and Military Affairs Commissioner Li Gang, also said that Xu Jingheng and Chao Shuozhi treated the promotions and demotions of great ministers as grounds for their own staying or leaving, harboring treachery and favoring private ties—and both were dismissed together.

sentences.zh: 安國言：「二人為去就，必有陳論。

translations.literal: Anguo said: "If the two took staying or leaving as their course, there must have been a memorial of argument.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo said, "If the two made staying or leaving their course, there must have been memorials setting forth their reasons.

sentences.zh: 懷奸徇私，必有實跡。

translations.literal: If they harbored treachery and favored private ties, there must have been concrete traces.
translations.idiomatic: If they harbored treachery and favored private ties, there must have been concrete evidence.

sentences.zh: 乞降付本省，載諸詞命。

translations.literal: I ask that [the charges] be sent down to this department and recorded in the appointment documents."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the charges be sent down to this department and recorded in the appointment documents."

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: No response.
translations.idiomatic: There was no response.

sentences.zh: 葉夢得知應天府，坐為蔡京所知，落職奉祠。

translations.literal: Ye Mengde, when he governed Yingtian Prefecture, was dismissed and given sacrificial appointment because he had been known to Cai Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Mengde, when he governed Yingtian Prefecture, was dismissed and given a sacrificial appointment because he had been known to Cai Jing.

sentences.zh: 安國言：「京罪已正，子孫編置，家財沒入，已無蔡氏矣。

translations.literal: Anguo said: "Cai Jing's crime has already been corrected; his descendants are registered and banished, family wealth confiscated—there is no longer a Cai clan.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo said, "Cai Jing's crime has already been corrected; his descendants have been registered and banished and his family wealth confiscated—there is no longer a Cai clan.

sentences.zh: 則向為京所引者，今皆朝廷之人，若更指為京黨，則人才見棄者眾，黨論何時而弭！

translations.literal: Then those formerly recommended by Jing are now all court people; if they are again labeled Jing faction members, then many talents will be cast away—when will factional strife cease!"
translations.idiomatic: Those who were formerly advanced by Jing are now all men of the court; if they are again labeled members of the Jing faction, then many talents will be cast aside—when will factional strife ever cease!"

sentences.zh: 」乃除夢得小郡。

translations.literal: [Anguo] then had Mengde appointed to a small prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo then had Mengde appointed to a small prefecture.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎何㮚建議分天下為四道，置四都總管，各付一面，以衛王室、捍強敵。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat He Bo proposed dividing the empire into four circuits, establishing four supreme commanders, each entrusted with one sector, to guard the royal house and repel strong enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat He Bo proposed dividing the empire into four circuits and establishing four supreme commanders, each entrusted with one sector, to guard the royal house and repel strong enemies.

sentences.zh: 安國言：「內外之勢，適平則安，偏重則危。

translations.literal: Anguo said: "The balance between inner and outer is: when level then secure, when weighted then perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo said, "The balance between inner and outer power is such that when it is level the state is secure, and when it is weighted to one side it becomes perilous.

sentences.zh: 今州郡太輕，理宜通變。

translations.literal: Now the prefectures and circuits are too light; it is right in principle to adapt flexibly.
translations.idiomatic: At present the prefectures and circuits are too lightly held; it is right in principle to adapt flexibly.

sentences.zh: 一旦以二十三路之廣，分為四道，事得專決，財得專用，官得辟置，兵得誅賞，權恐太重。

translations.literal: But at once to divide the breadth of twenty-three circuits into four circuits, with affairs decided exclusively, finances used exclusively, officials appointed exclusively, troops punished and rewarded exclusively—the power may be too great.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to divide at once the breadth of twenty-three circuits into four circuits, with exclusive power to decide affairs, use finances, appoint officials, and punish and reward troops—the authority may become too great.

sentences.zh: 萬一抗衡跋扈，何以待之？

translations.literal: If one day they contend and grow overbearing and insubordinate, how shall we deal with them?
translations.idiomatic: If one day they contend with the center and grow overbearing and insubordinate, how shall we deal with them?

sentences.zh: 乞據見今二十三路帥府，選擇重臣，付以都總管之權，專治軍旅。

translations.literal: I ask that based on the twenty-three circuit headquarters now in existence, heavy ministers be selected and entrusted with supreme commander authority, specializing in governing armies.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that, on the basis of the twenty-three circuit headquarters now in existence, heavy ministers be selected and entrusted with supreme commander authority, specializing in governing armies.

sentences.zh: 或有警急，即各率所屬守將應援，則一舉兩得矣。

translations.literal: If there is urgent alarm, each may lead subordinate defending generals to respond in aid—then one move gains two benefits."
translations.idiomatic: If there is urgent alarm, each may lead the defending generals under his command to respond in aid—then one move gains two benefits."

sentences.zh: 」尋以趙野總北道，安國言魏都地重，野必誤委寄。

translations.literal: Soon Zhao Ye was made supreme commander of the northern circuit; Anguo said the capital region of Wei was weighty in terrain and Ye would certainly mishandle the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhao Ye was made supreme commander of the northern circuit; Anguo said that the capital region of Wei was weighty in strategic importance and that Ye would certainly mishandle the commission.

sentences.zh: 是冬，金人大入，野遁，為群盜所殺，西道王襄擁眾不復北顧，如安國言。

translations.literal: That winter the Jurchens entered in force; Ye fled and was killed by bandits. Wang Xiang of the western circuit held the masses and no longer looked north—as Anguo had said.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Jurchens entered in force; Ye fled and was killed by bandits. Wang Xiang of the western circuit held his forces and no longer looked to the north—as Anguo had foretold.

sentences.zh: 李綱罷，中書舍人劉玨行詞，謂綱勇於報國，數至敗衄。

translations.literal: When Li Gang was dismissed, Drafting Attendant Liu Jue drafted the edict, saying Gang was brave in serving the state but had been defeated several times.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gang was dismissed, Drafting Attendant Liu Jue drafted the edict, saying that Gang was brave in serving the state but had suffered defeat several times.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎馮澥言玨為綱遊說，玨坐貶。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Feng Xi said Jue was lobbying for Gang; Jue was demoted on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Feng Xi said that Jue was lobbying for Gang, and Jue was demoted on that account.

sentences.zh: 安國封還詞頭，以為「侍從雖當獻納，至於彈擊官邪必歸風憲。

translations.literal: Anguo returned the edict draft, holding that "although attendants should offer advice, attacking official wrong must go to the censorial remonstrators.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo returned the edict draft, arguing that "although attendants should offer advice, the exposure of official wrongdoing must rest with the censorial remonstrators.

sentences.zh: 今台諫未有緘默不言之咎，而澥越職，此路若開，臣恐立於朝者各以好惡脅持傾陷，非所以靖朝著。

translations.literal: Now the remonstrators have no fault of silence and not speaking, yet Xi overstepped his office; if this path is opened, I fear those who stand at court will each use likes and dislikes to coerce, undermine, and topple one another—this is not the way to settle court demeanor."
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrators have committed no fault of silence, yet Xi overstepped his office. If this path is opened, I fear that those who stand at court will use likes and dislikes to coerce, undermine, and topple one another—this is not the way to settle the demeanor of the court."

sentences.zh: 」南仲大怒，何㮚從而擠之，詔與郡。

translations.literal: Nanzhong was greatly angered; He Bo joined in squeezing him out; an edict sent him to a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhong was greatly angered; He Bo joined in forcing him out, and an edict sent him to a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 㮚以安國素苦足疾，而海門地卑濕，乃除安國右文殿修撰、知通州。

translations.literal: Bo, because Anguo had long suffered foot ailment and Haimen was low and damp, appointed Anguo Right Wen Hall Compiler and prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Bo, knowing that Anguo had long suffered from foot ailment and that Haimen was low and damp, appointed Anguo Compiler of the Right Wen Hall and prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 安國在省一月，多在告之日，及出必有所論列。

translations.literal: Anguo in the central secretariat one month—most days were on sick leave; whenever he went out he invariably had something to memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: During the one month Anguo spent in the central secretariat, most days were spent on sick leave; yet whenever he did go out, he invariably had something to memorialize.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「事之小者，盍姑置之？

translations.literal: Someone said: "For small matters, why not for the time being set them aside?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to him, "For small matters, why not set them aside for the time being?"

sentences.zh: 」安國曰：「事之大者無不起於細微，今以小事為不必言，至於大事又不敢言，是無時而可言也！」

translations.literal: Anguo said: "Great matters all arise from minute beginnings; now if small matters are held not worth speaking of, when it comes to great matters one again dare not speak—then there is no time when one can speak!"
translations.idiomatic: Anguo said, "Great matters all arise from small beginnings. If small matters are held not worth speaking of, then when great matters come one again dares not speak—in the end there is no time when one can speak at all!"

sentences.zh: 安國既去逾旬，金人薄都城。

translations.literal: More than ten days after Anguo left, the Jurchens pressed close to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten days after Anguo left office, the Jurchens pressed close to the capital.

sentences.zh: 子寅為郎，在城中，客或憂之，安國愀然曰：「主上在重圍中，號令不出，卿大夫恨效忠無路，敢念子乎！

translations.literal: His son Yin was a court gentleman within the city; a guest worried for him; Anguo said gravely: "The sovereign is in heavy siege; orders do not issue; ministers hate that they have no road to show loyalty—how dare I think of my son!"
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin was a court gentleman within the city. When a guest worried for him, Anguo said gravely, "The sovereign is in heavy siege and orders do not issue; ministers resent that they have no road by which to show loyalty—how dare I think of my son!"

sentences.zh: 」敵圍益急，欽宗亟召安國及許景衡，詔竟不達。

translations.literal: The enemy siege grew urgent; Emperor Qinzong urgently summoned Anguo and Xu Jingheng, but the edict never reached them.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy siege grew more urgent; Emperor Qinzong urgently summoned Anguo and Xu Jingheng, but the edict never reached them.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，以給事中召。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne he was summoned as Supervisory Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, Anguo was summoned as Supervisory Attendant.

sentences.zh: 安國言：「昨因繳奏，遍觸權貴，今陛下將建中興，而政事弛張，人才升黜，尚未合宜，臣若一一行其職守，必以妄發，干犯典刑。

translations.literal: Anguo said: "Formerly because I submitted a remonstrance I broadly offended the powerful; now Your Majesty will establish restoration, yet governance is lax and tense, personnel promotions and demotions are still not fitting—if I carry out each duty of my office line by line, I will certainly be judged rash in speaking and violate statute."
translations.idiomatic: Anguo said, "Formerly, because I submitted a remonstrance, I broadly offended the powerful. Now Your Majesty is about to establish restoration, yet governance remains lax and inconsistent and the promotion and demotion of personnel are still not fitting. If I carry out each duty of my office in turn, I will certainly be judged rash in speaking and will violate statute."

sentences.zh: 」黃潛善諷給事中康執權論其托疾，罷之。

translations.literal: Huang Qianshan incited Supervisory Attendant Kang Zhiquan to say Anguo was feigning illness; he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Qianshan incited Supervisory Attendant Kang Zhiquan to accuse Anguo of feigning illness, and Anguo was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 三年，樞密張浚薦安國可大用，再除給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year Military Affairs Commissioner Zhang Jun recommended Anguo for great use; he was again appointed Supervisory Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Military Affairs Commissioner Zhang Jun recommended Anguo for great employment, and he was again appointed Supervisory Attendant.

sentences.zh: 賜其子起居郎寅手劄，令以上意催促。

translations.literal: [The emperor] granted his son Attendant Gentleman Yin a handwritten note, ordering him to convey the imperial intent and urge [Anguo] on.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted his son, Attendant Gentleman Yin, a handwritten note ordering him to convey the imperial intent and urge Anguo on.

sentences.zh: 既次池州，聞駕幸吳、越，引疾還。

translations.literal: Having reached Chizhou in sequence, hearing the imperial carriage was going to Wu and Yue, he pleaded illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Having reached Chizhou in due course, he heard that the imperial carriage was going to Wu and Yue and pleaded illness and returned.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，除中書舍人兼侍講，遣使趣召，安國以《時政論》二十一篇先獻之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing he was appointed Drafting Attendant with concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting; envoys were sent to urge summons; Anguo first presented his twenty-one Treatises on Current Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxing he was appointed Drafting Attendant with concurrent service as Lecturer-in-Waiting; envoys were sent to urge his summons, and Anguo first presented his twenty-one Treatises on Current Affairs.

sentences.zh: 論入，復除給事中。

translations.literal: When the treatises entered he was again appointed Supervisory Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the treatises were submitted, he was again appointed Supervisory Attendant.

sentences.zh: 二年七月入對，高宗曰：「聞卿大名，渴於相見，何為累詔不至？

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year he faced the throne; Emperor Gaozong said: "I have heard your great name and thirst to meet you—why have you not come after repeated edicts?"
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year he faced the throne. Emperor Gaozong said, "I have long heard your great name and have thirsted to meet you—why have you not come after repeated edicts?"

sentences.zh: 」安國辭謝，乞以所進二十一篇者施行。

translations.literal: Anguo declined with thanks and asked that the twenty-one pieces presented be put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo declined with thanks and asked that the twenty-one pieces he had presented be put into practice.

sentences.zh: 其論之目，曰《定計》、《建都》、《設險》、《制國》、《恤民》、《立政》、《核實》、《尚志》、《正心》、《養氣》、《宏度》、《寬隱》。

translations.literal: The headings of his treatises were: Settling the Plan, Establishing the Capital, Setting Defenses, Ordering the State, Cherishing the People, Establishing Government, Verifying Facts, Upholding Purpose, Rectifying the Mind, Nourishing Qi, Magnanimity, Magnanimous Reticence.
translations.idiomatic: The headings of his treatises were Settling the Plan, Establishing the Capital, Setting Defenses, Ordering the State, Cherishing the People, Establishing Government, Verifying Facts, Upholding Purpose, Rectifying the Mind, Nourishing Qi, Magnanimity, and Magnanimous Reticence.

sentences.zh: 論《定計》略曰：「陛下履極六年，以建都，則未有必守不移之居；

translations.literal: On Settling the Plan in brief: "Your Majesty has been on the throne six years—for establishing the capital, yet there is no residence that must be held and not moved from;
translations.idiomatic: On Settling the Plan he wrote in brief, "Your Majesty has been on the throne six years, yet for establishing the capital there is still no residence that must be held and not abandoned;

sentences.zh: 以討賊，則未有必操不變之術；

translations.literal: for suppressing the bandits, yet there is no tactic that must be held and not changed;
translations.idiomatic: for suppressing the bandits, there is still no tactic that must be held and not changed;

sentences.zh: 以立政，則未有必行不反之令；

translations.literal: for establishing government, yet there is no order that must be carried out and not reversed;
translations.idiomatic: for establishing government, there is still no order that must be carried out and not reversed;

sentences.zh: 以任官，則未有必信不疑之臣。

translations.literal: for employing officials, yet there is no minister who must be trusted without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: for employing officials, there is still no minister who must be trusted without doubt.

sentences.zh: 舍今不圖，後悔何及！

translations.literal: If we do not plan now, what regret will there be later!"
translations.idiomatic: If we do not plan now, what regret will there be later!"

sentences.zh: 」論《建都》謂：「宜定都建康以比關中、河內，為興復之基。

translations.literal: On Establishing the Capital he said: "The capital should be fixed at Jiankang to compare with Guanzhong and Henei as the base of restoration."
translations.idiomatic: On Establishing the Capital he said, "The capital should be fixed at Jiankang, to stand with Guanzhong and Henei as the base of restoration."

sentences.zh: 」論《設險》謂：「欲固上流，必保漢、沔；

translations.literal: On Setting Defenses he said: "To secure the upper reaches one must hold Han and Mian;
translations.idiomatic: On Setting Defenses he said, "To secure the upper reaches one must hold Han and Mian;

sentences.zh: 欲固下流，必守淮、泗；

translations.literal: to secure the lower reaches one must defend Huai and Si;
translations.idiomatic: to secure the lower reaches one must defend the Huai and the Si;

sentences.zh: 欲固中流，必以重兵鎮安陸。

translations.literal: to secure the middle reaches one must with heavy troops garrison Anlu."
translations.idiomatic: to secure the middle reaches one must station heavy troops at Anlu."

sentences.zh: 」論《尚志》謂：「當必志於恢復中原，祗奉陵寢；

translations.literal: On Upholding Purpose he said: "One must resolve to recover the Central Plain and reverently tend the imperial tombs;
translations.idiomatic: On Upholding Purpose he said, "One must resolve to recover the Central Plain and reverently tend the imperial tombs;

sentences.zh: 必志於掃平仇敵，迎復兩宮。

translations.literal: must resolve to sweep away the enemy and welcome back the two palaces."
translations.idiomatic: and must resolve to sweep away the enemy and welcome back the two palaces."

sentences.zh: 」論《正心》謂：「戡定禍亂，雖急於戎務，而裁決戎務，必本於方寸。

translations.literal: On Rectifying the Mind he said: "Though quelling calamity and disorder is urgent with military affairs, yet to decide military affairs the root lies in the inch-square [mind].
translations.idiomatic: On Rectifying the Mind he said, "Though quelling calamity and disorder is urgent and military affairs press upon us, to decide military affairs the root lies in the inch-square mind.

sentences.zh: 願選正臣多聞識、有志慮、敢直言者置諸左右，日夕討論，以宅厥心。

translations.literal: I wish upright ministers of much learning, purpose, and daring to speak directly placed at left and right, discussing day and night, to settle his heart."
translations.idiomatic: I wish that upright ministers of broad learning, firm purpose, and daring to speak directly be placed at his left and right to discuss day and night and settle his heart."

sentences.zh: 」論《養氣》謂：「用兵之勝負，軍旅之強弱，將帥之勇怯，係人君所養之氣曲直何如。

translations.literal: On Nourishing Qi he said: "Victory and defeat in using troops, strength and weakness of armies, courage and cowardice of generals depend on the straightness or crookedness of the qi the ruler nourishes—how is it?
translations.idiomatic: On Nourishing Qi he said, "Victory and defeat in using troops, the strength and weakness of armies, and the courage and cowardice of generals all depend on whether the qi the ruler nourishes is straight or crooked.

sentences.zh: 願強於為善，益新厥德，使信於諸夏、聞於夷狄者，無曲可議，則至剛可以塞兩間，一怒可以安天下矣。

translations.literal: I wish to be strong in doing good and ever renew virtue, so that trust among the states and renown among the barbarians have no crookedness to discuss—then the utmost rigidity can fill between Heaven and Earth, one wrath can settle the realm."
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty to be strong in doing good and ever to renew his virtue, so that what the states trust and the barbarians hear has no crookedness that can be discussed—then the utmost rigidity can fill the space between Heaven and Earth, and one burst of wrath can settle the realm."

sentences.zh: 」安國嘗謂：「雖諸葛復生，為今日計，不能易此論也。」

translations.literal: Anguo once said: "Even if Zhuge Liang were reborn, for today's reckoning this doctrine cannot be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Anguo once said, "Even if Zhuge Liang were reborn, for the reckoning of this day this doctrine could not be changed."

sentences.zh: 居旬日，再見，以疾懇求去。

translations.literal: After ten days in post he was received again; he earnestly begged to leave on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days in office he was received again and earnestly begged to leave on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 高宗曰：「聞卿深於《春秋》，方欲講論。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong said: "I hear you are deep in the Spring and Autumn; I am just about to lecture on it."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong said, "I hear that you are deeply versed in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and I am just about to lecture on it."

sentences.zh: 」遂以《左氏傳》付安國點句正音。

translations.literal: He then handed the Zuo Commentary to Anguo to punctuate sentences and correct pronunciation.
translations.idiomatic: He then handed the Zuo Commentary to Anguo to punctuate the text and correct the pronunciation.

sentences.zh: 安國奏：「《春秋》經世大典，見諸行事，非空言比。

translations.literal: Anguo memorialized: "The Spring and Autumn is the great canon for ordering generations, seen in conduct—not comparable to empty words.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo memorialized, "The Spring and Autumn Annals is the great canon for ordering the ages; its meaning is seen in conduct and is not to be compared with empty words.

sentences.zh: 今方思濟艱難，《左氏》繁碎，不宜虛費光陰，耽玩文采，莫若潛心聖經。

translations.literal: Now we are just thinking to cross hardship; the Zuo is cumbersome and fragmentary, unfit to waste bright hours indulging in literary ornament—better to concentrate the mind on the sage classics."
translations.idiomatic: Now we are only beginning to think of crossing hardship; the Zuo Commentary is cumbersome and fragmentary and unfit for wasting bright hours in literary ornament. Better to concentrate the mind on the sage classics."

sentences.zh: 」高宗稱善。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong praised this.

sentences.zh: 尋除安國兼侍讀，專講《春秋》。

translations.literal: Soon Anguo was appointed concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting, lecturing exclusively on the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Anguo was appointed concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting and lectured exclusively on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 時講官四人，援例乞各專一經。

translations.literal: At the time four lecturers petitioned by precedent that each specialize in one classic.
translations.idiomatic: At the time four lecturers petitioned that, by precedent, each should specialize in one classic.

sentences.zh: 高宗曰：「他人通經，豈胡安國比。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong said: "When others penetrate classics, how can they compare with Hu Anguo?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong said, "When others penetrate the classics, how can they compare with Hu Anguo?"

sentences.zh: 」不許。

translations.literal: He did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 會除故相朱勝非同都督江、淮、荊、浙諸軍事，安國奏：「勝非與黃潛善、汪伯彥同在政府，緘默附會，循致渡江。

translations.literal: When former Chief Councillor Zhu Shengnon was appointed concurrent military commander of Jiang, Huai, Jing, and Zhe circuits, Anguo memorialized: "Shengnon was in government with Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan, silent and in accord, leading step by step to crossing the river.
translations.idiomatic: When the former chief councillor Zhu Shengnon was appointed concurrent military commander of the Jiang, Huai, Jing, and Zhe circuits, Anguo memorialized, "Shengnon was in government with Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan, silent and in accord, and led step by step to the crossing of the river.

sentences.zh: 尊用張邦昌結好金國，淪滅三綱，天下憤鬱。

translations.literal: He honored Zhang Bangchang and made friendly terms with the Jin state, destroying the three bonds—under Heaven there was rage and depression.
translations.idiomatic: He honored Zhang Bangchang and made friendly terms with the Jin state, destroying the three bonds of human order, and under Heaven there was rage and depression.

sentences.zh: 及正位塚司，苗、劉肆逆，貪生苟容，辱逮君父。

translations.literal: When he reached the post of chief minister, Miao and Liu committed outrage; greedy for life he was accommodating, shame reaching ruler and father.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the post of chief minister, Miao and Liu committed outrage; greedy for life, he was accommodating, and shame reached to ruler and father.

sentences.zh: 今強敵憑陵，叛臣不忌，用人得失，係國安危，深恐勝非上誤大計。

translations.literal: Now strong enemies press the borders, rebellious ministers heed no restraint; gain and loss in employing men ties to the state's safety or peril—I deeply fear Shengnon above will mislead the great plan."
translations.idiomatic: Now strong enemies press upon the borders and rebellious ministers heed no restraint. Gain and loss in employing men is tied to the safety or peril of the state, and I deeply fear that Shengnon above will mislead the great plan."

sentences.zh: 」勝非改除侍讀，安國持錄黃不下，左相呂頤浩特令檢正黃龜年書行。

translations.literal: Shengnon was changed to Lecturer-in-Waiting; Anguo held the recorded yellow and would not issue it; Left Councillor Lü Yihao specially ordered Compiler Huang Guinian to sign and execute.
translations.idiomatic: Shengnon was changed to Lecturer-in-Waiting; Anguo held the recorded yellow and would not issue it; Left Councillor Lü Yihao specially ordered Compiler Huang Guinian to sign and execute the appointment.

sentences.zh: 安國言：「『有官守者，不得其職則去』。

translations.literal: Anguo said: "'Those who have an official charge—if they do not obtain their function, then leave.'
translations.idiomatic: Anguo said, "'Those who hold an official charge, if they do not obtain their function, then leave.'

sentences.zh: 臣今待罪無補，既失其職，當去甚明。

translations.literal: Your servant now bears charge without supplement, having already lost function; to leave is very clear.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant now bears charge without supplement and has already lost his function; that he should leave is very clear.

sentences.zh: 況勝非係臣論列之人，今朝廷乃稱勝非處苗、劉之變，能調護聖躬。

translations.literal: Moreover Shengnon is a man your servant has listed in discussion; now the court yet says Shengnon in Miao and Liu's change could soothe and protect the sacred person.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Shengnon is a man whom your servant has listed in discussion, yet now the court says that in Miao and Liu's outrage Shengnon was able to soothe and protect the sacred person.

sentences.zh: 昔公羊氏言祭仲廢君為行權，先儒力排其說。

translations.literal: Formerly the Gongyang school said that Zhong of Cai deposing the ruler was exercising expedient power; earlier Confucians strenuously rejected this doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Gongyang school said that Zhong of Cai, in deposing his ruler, was exercising expedient power, but the earlier Confucians strenuously rejected this doctrine.

sentences.zh: 蓋權宜廢置非所施於君父，《春秋》大法，尤謹於此。

translations.literal: Expedient suspension and installation is not applied to ruler and father; the great law of the Spring and Autumn is especially strict here.
translations.idiomatic: Expedient suspension and installation is not to be applied to ruler and father; the great law of the Spring and Autumn Annals is especially strict on this point.

sentences.zh: 建炎之失節者，今雖特釋而不問，又加選擢，習俗既成，大非君父之利。

translations.literal: Those who failed in propriety in Jianyan are now specially released without inquiry, yet again promoted and selected—once custom is formed, this greatly harms the benefit of ruler and father.
translations.idiomatic: Those who failed in propriety during the Jianyan era are now specially released without inquiry and yet again promoted and selected. Once such custom is formed, it greatly harms the benefit of ruler and father.

sentences.zh: 臣以《春秋》入侍，而與勝非為列，有違經訓。

translations.literal: Your servant enters attendance with the Spring and Autumn yet is in the same row as Shengnon—this violates scripture and instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant enters attendance with the Spring and Autumn Annals yet sits in the same row as Shengnon—this violates scripture and instruction."

sentences.zh: 」遂臥家不出。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he lay at home and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he kept to his home and would not go out.

sentences.zh: 初，頤浩都督江上還朝，欲去異己者，未得其策。

translations.literal: Initially, when Yihao returned to court from commanding on the river, he wished to remove those unlike himself but had not obtained a strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Lü Yihao returned to court after commanding on the Yangzi, he wished to remove those who opposed him but had not yet found a strategy.

sentences.zh: 或教之指為朋黨，且曰：「黨魁在瑣闈，當先去之。

translations.literal: Someone advised him to point to them as a faction, and said: "The faction leader is in the privy chamber; he should first be removed.
