translations.idiomatic: Someone advised him to charge them with forming a faction, saying, "The ringleader sits in the privy chamber and should be removed first.

sentences.zh: 」頤浩大喜，即引勝非為助，而降旨曰：「胡安國屢召，偃蹇不至，今始造朝，又數有請。

translations.literal: " Yihao was greatly pleased, immediately brought Shengnon as help, and issued an edict saying: "Hu Anguo was repeatedly summoned, proud and slow and did not arrive; now he first comes to court, and again has many requests.
translations.idiomatic: " Yihao was greatly pleased. He immediately enlisted Shengnon's aid and issued an edict saying, "Hu Anguo was summoned many times yet held himself aloof and would not come. Now he finally appears at court and again makes repeated demands.

sentences.zh: 初言勝非不可同都督，及改命經筵，又以為非，豈不以時艱不肯盡瘁，乃欲求微罪而去，其自為謀則善，如國計何？

translations.literal: At first he said Shengnon could not serve together as military commander; when the appointment was changed to the royal lecture hall, again he thought it wrong. Is it not that because times are hard he refuses full exhaustion, and instead seeks petty offenses by which to leave? His planning for himself is good, but what of the state plan?
translations.idiomatic: First he said that Shengnon could not serve alongside him as military commander; when the appointment was changed to the royal lecture hall, he again found fault. Does he not, because of these hard times, refuse to exert himself to the utmost and instead seek petty offenses as grounds to withdraw? That may serve his own interests well enough, but what of the interests of the realm?

sentences.zh: 」落職，提舉仙都觀。

translations.literal: " [Anguo] was stripped of office and appointed supervisor of Xiandu Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: " Anguo was removed from office and appointed supervisor of Xiandu Abbey.

sentences.zh: 是夕，彗出東南。

translations.literal: That evening, a comet appeared in the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: That same evening, a comet appeared in the southeast.

sentences.zh: 右相秦檜三上章乞留之，不報，即解相印去。

translations.literal: Right Councillor Qin Hui thrice submitted memorials begging to retain [Anguo]; there was no response, and he immediately relinquished the seal of councillor and left.
translations.idiomatic: Right Councilor Qin Hui submitted three memorials begging that Anguo be kept in office, but received no reply and at once surrendered the councilor's seal and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 侍御史江躋上疏，極言勝非不可用，安國不當責。

translations.literal: Supervisory Censor Jiang Ji submitted a memorial, speaking at length that Shengnon could not be employed and Anguo should not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory Censor Jiang Ji submitted a memorial saying emphatically that Shengnon was unfit for office and that Anguo should not be punished.

sentences.zh: 右司諫吳表臣亦言安國扶病見君，欲行所學，今無故罪去，恐非所以示天下。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Official Wu Biaochen also said Anguo attended the ruler while supporting illness, wishing to put his learning into practice; now without cause he is punished and removed—perhaps this is not how to show the world.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official Wu Biaochen also said that Anguo had attended the emperor despite illness because he wished to put his learning into practice, and that to punish and remove him without cause would perhaps not be the right way to show the world.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: There was no reply.

sentences.zh: 頤浩即黜給事中程瑀、起居舍人張燾及躋等二十餘人，云應天變除舊布新之象。

translations.literal: Yihao immediately dismissed Supervising Secretary Cheng Yu, Attendant Gentleman for Court Audiences Zhang Zhao, and Jiang Ji and more than twenty others, saying this responded to Heaven's change to remove the old and spread the new.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao immediately dismissed Supervising Secretary Cheng Yu, Attendant Gentleman for Court Audiences Zhang Zhao, Jiang Ji, and more than twenty others, saying this answered the heavenly sign of casting off the old and ushering in the new.

sentences.zh: 台省一空，勝非遂相，安國竟歸。

translations.literal: The censorate and secretariat were emptied; Shengnon then became councillor; Anguo ultimately returned.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate and secretariat were emptied at a stroke; Shengnon then became chief councilor; and Anguo returned home at last.

sentences.zh: 五年，除徽猷閣待制、知永州，安國辭。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was appointed Awaiting Draft in the Huiyou Pavilion and prefect of Yongzhou; Anguo declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed Awaiting Draft in the Huiyou Pavilion and prefect of Yongzhou, but Anguo declined.

sentences.zh: 詔以經筵舊臣，重閔勞之，特從其請，提舉江州太平觀，令纂修所著《春秋傳》。

translations.literal: An edict [said that] as an old minister of the royal lecture hall, deeply sympathizing and rewarding his labors, [the throne] especially granted his request, appointing him to administer Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou, ordering him to compile and revise his authored Commentary on the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: An edict held that, as a former lecturer at the royal lecture hall, his labors deserved special sympathy and reward. The court granted his request, appointing him to administer Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou and ordering him to compile and revise his Commentary on the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 書成，高宗謂深得聖人之旨，除提舉萬壽觀兼侍讀。

translations.literal: When the book was finished, Gaozong said it deeply obtained the sage's intent; [Anguo] was appointed supervisor of Wanshou Abbey with concurrent appointment as Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, Gaozong said that it had fully grasped the intent of the sage. Anguo was appointed supervisor of Wanshou Abbey with concurrent appointment as Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 未行，諫官陳公輔上疏詆假托程頤之學者。

translations.literal: Before he took office, remonstrance official Chen Gongfu submitted a memorial slandering those who falsely borrowed the learning of Cheng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, Remonstrance Official Chen Gongfu submitted a memorial attacking those who falsely claimed the learning of Cheng Yi.

sentences.zh: 安國奏曰：「孔、孟之道不傳久矣，自頤兄弟始發明之，然後知其可學而至。

translations.literal: Anguo memorialized: "The way of Confucius and Mencius has long not been transmitted; from the Cheng brothers it was first brought forth, and only then did one know it could be learned and attained.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo memorialized, "The way of Confucius and Mencius has long ceased to be transmitted. It was first recovered by the Cheng brothers, and only then did men know that it could be learned and attained.

sentences.zh: 今使學者師孔、孟，而禁不得從頤學，是入室而不由戶。

translations.literal: Now to have scholars take Confucius and Mencius as masters yet forbid them from following Yi's learning is like entering a room not through the door.
translations.idiomatic: If scholars are told to take Confucius and Mencius as their masters yet forbidden to follow the learning of Cheng Yi, that is like entering a house without going through the door.

sentences.zh: 本朝自嘉祐以來，西都有邵雍、程顥及其弟頤，關中有張載，皆以道德名世，公卿大夫所欽慕而師尊之。

translations.literal: Since Jiayou in this dynasty, in the western capital were Shao Yong, Cheng Hao and his younger brother Yi, in Guanzhong was Zhang Zai—all famed the age for virtue and the Way, admired and honored as teachers by grandees and great officers.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jiayou era of this dynasty, Shao Yong, Cheng Hao, and his younger brother Cheng Yi were in the western capital, and Zhang Zai was in Guanzhong. All were famed throughout the age for virtue and the Way, and grandees and great officers admired and honored them as teachers.

sentences.zh: 會王安石、蔡京等曲加排抑，故其道不行。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi, Cai Jing and others repeatedly bent to suppress them, therefore their Way did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: But Wang Anshi, Cai Jing, and others persistently forced them down and suppressed them, so their Way could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 望下禮官討論故事，加之封爵，載在祀典，比於荀、楊、韓氏，仍詔館閣裒其遺書，校正頒行，使邪說者不得作。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will order the rites officials to discuss precedent, add them titles of enfeoffment, record them in the sacrificial canon, comparing them to the houses of Xun, Yang, and Han, and also decree that the institutes and libraries collect their surviving books, correct and promulgate them, so that heterodox doctrines cannot arise.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to order the rites officials to consult precedent, grant them posthumous titles, and record them in the sacrificial canon alongside the houses of Xun, Yang, and Han; and also to decree that the palace institutes gather their surviving writings, correct them, and promulgate them, so that perverse doctrines cannot arise.

sentences.zh: 」奏入，公輔與中丞周秘、侍御史石公揆承望宰相風旨，交章論安國學術頗僻。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, Gongfu together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhou Mi and Supervisory Censor Shi Gongkui, hoping for the chief minister's intent, submitted memorials in succession saying Anguo's learning was rather heterodox.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, Gongfu, together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhou Mi and Supervisory Censor Shi Gongkui—reading the chief minister's wishes—submitted memorial after memorial declaring that Anguo's learning was rather heterodox.

sentences.zh: 除知永州，辭，復提舉太平觀，進寶文閣直學士，卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Yongzhou, declined, again appointed to administer Taiping Abbey, advanced to Direct Academic Scholar of the Baowen Pavilion, died, age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Yongzhou but declined, was again appointed to administer Taiping Abbey, was promoted to Direct Academic Scholar of the Baowen Pavilion, and died at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 詔贈四官，又降詔加賻，賜田十頃恤其孤，諡曰文定，蓋非常格也。

translations.literal: An edict granted posthumously four offices; again an edict was issued adding condolence gifts, bestowing ten qing of fields to support his orphans; posthumous title Wending—this was not the ordinary measure.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him posthumously four offices. Another edict added condolence gifts and bestowed ten qing of fields to support his orphaned family. His posthumous title was Wending—far beyond the usual measure.

sentences.zh: 安國強學力行，以聖人為標的，志於康濟時艱，見中原淪沒，遺黎塗炭，常若痛切於其身。

translations.literal: Anguo strongly pursued learning and vigorously practiced, taking the sage as his mark, resolved to relieve the hard times, seeing the Central Plains lost, the remnant people in torment—as if the pain cut into his own person.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo pursued learning with vigor and put it into practice, taking the sage as his standard and setting his heart on relieving the hardships of the age. When he saw the Central Plains overrun and the remnant people plunged into misery, it was as if the pain cut into his own flesh.

sentences.zh: 雖數以罪去，其愛君憂國之心遠而彌篤，每有君命，即置家事不問。

translations.literal: Though repeatedly removed on charges, his heart of loving the ruler and worrying for the state grew more steadfast with distance; whenever there was a ruler's command, he immediately set aside family matters without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Though he was repeatedly dismissed under accusations, his love of the ruler and concern for the state only grew deeper and steadier with time. Whenever the emperor commanded him, he at once set aside his family affairs without a second thought.

sentences.zh: 然風度凝遠，蕭然塵表，視天下萬物無一足以嬰其心。

translations.literal: Yet his bearing was solemn and far-reaching, austere beyond the dusty world; he viewed all things under Heaven and not one was enough to ensnare his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his bearing was lofty and remote, austere and aloof from the dusty world. Of all things under Heaven, not one was enough to entangle his heart.

sentences.zh: 自登第迄謝事，四十年在官，實曆不及六載。

translations.literal: From passing the examination until resigning office, forty years in official life—actual years of service did not reach six.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he passed the examinations until he left office, forty years passed in official life, yet the actual years he served did not reach six.

sentences.zh: 朱震被召，問出處之宜，安國曰：「子發學《易》二十年，此事當素定矣。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhen was summoned and asked about the proper course of taking or leaving office. Anguo said: "Zifa, you have studied the Changes twenty years—on this matter you should long since have been settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Zhen was summoned and asked about the proper course of taking or leaving office, Anguo said, "Zifa, you have studied the Changes for twenty years. On a matter such as this, you should long since have settled your mind.

sentences.zh: 世間惟講學論政，不可不切切詢究，至於行己大致，去就語默之幾，如人飲食，其饑飽寒溫，必自斟酌，不可決諸人，亦非人所能決也。

translations.literal: In the world only matters of lecturing on learning and discussing government cannot but be urgently inquired into and examined; as for the great outline of self-conduct, the subtle points of going or staying, speaking or silent—as with human eating and drinking, hunger and fullness, cold and warmth, one must oneself weigh them and cannot decide them by others, nor can others decide them either.
translations.idiomatic: In worldly affairs, only questions of lecturing on learning and debating policy must be pursued urgently and examined closely. But as for the broad principles of personal conduct—the fine distinctions of going or staying, speaking or remaining silent—these are like eating and drinking: hunger and fullness, cold and warmth must be weighed by oneself. They cannot be decided for you by others, nor can anyone else decide them on your behalf.

sentences.zh: 吾平生出處皆內斷於心，浮世利名如蠛蠓過前，何足道哉！

translations.literal: My whole life's course of entering or leaving has been internally decided in the heart; the floating world's profit and fame are like gnats passing before the eyes—how are they worth speaking of!
translations.idiomatic: Throughout my life I have decided for myself, inwardly, whether to serve or withdraw. The profit and fame of this floating world are like gnats darting past the eyes—what are they worth mentioning!

sentences.zh: 」故渡江以來，儒者進退合義，以安國、尹焞為稱首。

translations.literal: " Therefore since crossing the river, among Confucians whose advancement and withdrawal accord with righteousness, Anguo and Yin Chun are chiefly praised.
translations.idiomatic: " That is why, since the crossing of the Yangzi, among scholars whose advances and withdrawals accord with righteousness, Anguo and Yin Chun have been chiefly praised.

sentences.zh: 侯仲良言必稱二程先生，他無所許可。

translations.literal: Hou Zhongliang in speech always named the two Masters Cheng; he approved of no one else.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhongliang always spoke of the two Masters Cheng and approved of no one else.

sentences.zh: 後見安國，歎曰：「吾以為志在天下，視不義富貴真如浮雲者，二程先生而已，不意復有斯人也。」

translations.literal: Later, when he saw Anguo, he sighed and said: "I thought that those who set their hearts on the realm and regarded unrighteous wealth and honor as truly floating clouds were only the two Masters Cheng—I did not expect there would be such a man as this."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he met Anguo, he sighed and said, "I thought that only the two Masters Cheng set their hearts on the realm and regarded unrighteous wealth and honor as truly floating clouds. I did not expect to find such a man again.

sentences.zh: 安國所與遊者，遊酢、謝良佐、楊時皆程門高弟。

translations.literal: Those with whom Anguo associated were You Zuo, Xie Liangzuo, and Yang Shi—all eminent disciples of the Cheng school.
translations.idiomatic: Those with whom Anguo associated were You Zuo, Xie Liangzuo, and Yang Shi, all eminent disciples of the Cheng school.

sentences.zh: 良佐嘗語人曰：「胡康侯如大冬嚴雪，百草萎死，而松柏挺然獨秀者也。

translations.literal: Liangzuo once said to others: "Hu Kanghou is like great winter and severe snow: the hundred grasses wither and die, yet pine and cypress stand upright alone in splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzuo once said to others, "Hu Kanghou is like the deep winter under heavy snow: the hundred grasses wither and die, yet pine and cypress stand upright alone in splendor.

sentences.zh: 」安國之使湖北也，時方為府教授，良佐為應城宰，安國質疑訪道，禮之甚恭，每來謁而去，必端笏正立目送之。

translations.literal: " When Anguo went to Hubei, Shi was then professor of the prefecture, and Liangzuo was magistrate of Yingcheng; Anguo questioned him and sought the Way, treating him with great respect—each time he came to call and then left, [Anguo] would hold his tablet upright and stand properly, seeing him off with his gaze.
translations.idiomatic: When Anguo was posted to Hubei, Yang Shi was then professor of the prefectural school and Liangzuo was magistrate of Yingcheng. Anguo questioned him and sought instruction in the Way, treating him with great respect. Each time Liangzuo came to call and then departed, Anguo would hold his tablet upright, stand properly, and see him off with his gaze.

sentences.zh: 自王安石廢《春秋》不列於學官，安國謂：「先聖手所筆削之書，乃使人主不得聞講說，學士不得相傳習，亂倫滅理，用夏變夷，殆由乎此。

translations.literal: Since Wang Anshi removed the Spring and Autumn from the list of classics taught in the official schools, Anguo said: "The book that the former sage personally edited with his own hand—yet the ruler is made unable to hear it lectured upon and scholars unable to transmit and study it—disordering human bonds and extinguishing principle, using Xia to transform into Yi: this is perhaps where it begins.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wang Anshi removed the Spring and Autumn Annals from the classics taught in the official schools, Anguo said, "The book that the former sage personally edited with his own hand—yet the ruler is made unable to hear it lectured upon and scholars unable to transmit and study it—disordering human bonds and extinguishing principle, using Xia to transform into Yi: this is perhaps where it begins.

sentences.zh: 」故潛心是書二十餘年，以為天下事物無不備於此。

translations.literal: " Therefore he devoted his heart to this book for more than twenty years, taking it that nothing under Heaven was not fully contained in it.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he devoted his heart to this book for more than twenty years, believing that nothing under Heaven was not fully contained within it.

sentences.zh: 每歎曰：「此傳心要典也。」

translations.literal: He often sighed and said: "This is the essential canon for transmitting the heart-mind."
translations.idiomatic: He often sighed and said, "This is the essential canon for transmitting the heart-mind.

sentences.zh: 安國少欲以文章名世，既學道，乃不復措意。

translations.literal: In youth Anguo wished to make a name in letters; once he studied the Way, he no longer gave it thought.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Anguo wished to make a name for himself in letters; once he studied the Way, he no longer gave it thought.

sentences.zh: 有文集十五卷、《資治通鑒舉要補遺》一百卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in fifteen juan and Essentials and Supplements to the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance in one hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in fifteen juan and Essentials and Supplements to the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance in one hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 三子，寅、宏、寧。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Yin, Hong, and Ning.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Yin, Hong, and Ning.

translations.literal: 〈Sons〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Sons〉

sentences.zh: 寅

translations.literal: Yin
translations.idiomatic: Yin

sentences.zh: 寅字明仲，安國弟之子也。

translations.literal: Yin, styled Mingzhong, was the son of Anguo's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, whose courtesy name was Mingzhong, was the son of Anguo's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 寅將生，弟婦以多男欲不舉，安國妻夢大魚躍盆水中，急往取而子之。

translations.literal: When Yin was about to be born, his younger brother's wife, because she already had many sons, wished not to raise the child; Anguo's wife dreamed of a great fish leaping in a basin of water, hurried to take it, and raised the boy.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin was about to be born, his younger brother's wife, because she already had many sons, wished not to raise the child. Anguo's wife dreamed of a great fish leaping in a basin of water, hurried to take it, and raised the boy herself.

sentences.zh: 少桀黠難制，父閉之空閣，其上有雜木，寅盡刻為人形。

translations.literal: In youth he was fierce and cunning and hard to control; his father shut him in an empty loft, above which were miscellaneous trees; Yin carved them all into human figures.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was fierce and cunning and hard to control. His father shut him in an empty loft, above which were miscellaneous trees, and Yin carved them all into human figures.

sentences.zh: 安國曰：「當有以移其心。

translations.literal: Anguo said: "There must be a way to shift his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo said, "There must be a way to shift his heart.

sentences.zh: 」別置書數千卷於其上，年餘，寅悉成誦，不遺一卷。

translations.literal: " He separately placed several thousand volumes of books above [the loft]; after more than a year, Yin had memorized them all completely, not leaving out a single volume.
translations.idiomatic: " He placed several thousand volumes of books above the loft. After more than a year, Yin had memorized them all completely, not leaving out a single volume.

sentences.zh: 遊辟雍，中宣和進士甲科。

translations.literal: He studied at the Imperial College and passed the jinshi examination in the first rank in the Xuanhe era.
translations.idiomatic: He studied at the Imperial College and passed the jinshi examination in the first rank in the Xuanhe era.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，以御史中丞何㮚薦，召除秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingkang era, on the recommendation of Vice Censor-in-Chief He Li, he was summoned and appointed collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingkang era, on the recommendation of Vice Censor-in-Chief He Li, he was summoned and appointed collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 楊時為祭酒，寅從之受學。

translations.literal: Yang Shi was then director of the Imperial College, and Yin received instruction from him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shi was then director of the Imperial College, and Yin received instruction from him.

sentences.zh: 遷司門員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue for the Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue for the Gate.

sentences.zh: 金人陷京師，議立異姓，寅與張浚、趙鼎逃太學中，不書議狀。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens took the capital, there was discussion of enthroning a man of another surname; Yin, together with Zhang Jun and Zhao Ding, fled into the Imperial College and did not sign the deliberation document.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens took the capital, there was discussion of enthroning a man of another surname. Yin, together with Zhang Jun and Zhao Ding, fled into the Imperial College and did not sign the deliberation document.

sentences.zh: 張邦昌偽立，寅棄官歸，言者劾其離次，降一官。

translations.literal: When Zhang Bangchang was falsely enthroned, Yin abandoned his office and returned home; accusers impeached him for leaving his post and he was demoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Bangchang was falsely enthroned, Yin abandoned his office and returned home. Accusers impeached him for leaving his post, and he was demoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，高宗幸金陵，樞密使張浚薦為駕部郎官，尋擢起居郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan, when Gaozong visited Jinling, Military Affairs Commissioner Zhang Jun recommended him as chariot-section officer; soon he was promoted to Attendant Gentleman for Court Audiences.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyan, when Gaozong visited Jinling, Military Affairs Commissioner Zhang Jun recommended him as chariot-section officer; soon he was promoted to Attendant Gentleman for Court Audiences.

sentences.zh: 金人南侵，詔議移蹕之所，寅上書曰：

translations.literal: When the Jurchens invaded south, an edict ordered discussion of where to move the traveling court; Yin submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens invaded south, an edict ordered discussion of where to move the traveling court. Yin submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 昨陛下以親王、介弟出師河北，二聖既遷，則當糾合義師，北向迎請。

translations.literal: Yesterday Your Majesty, as imperial prince and younger brother of the emperor, went forth as commander to Hebei; once the Two Emperors had been removed, then one ought to gather righteous armies and turn north to welcome and escort them back.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday Your Majesty, as imperial prince and younger brother of the emperor, went forth as commander to Hebei. Once the Two Emperors had been removed, you ought to have gathered righteous armies and turned north to welcome and escort them back.

sentences.zh: 而遽膺翊戴，亟居尊位，斬戮直臣，以杜言路。

translations.literal: Yet you hastily accepted support and elevation, quickly took the exalted seat, executed upright ministers, and blocked the road of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you hastily accepted support and elevation, quickly took the exalted seat, executed upright ministers, and blocked the road of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 南巡淮海，偷安歲月，敵入關陝，漫不捍禦。

translations.literal: You toured south to the Huai and sea regions, stealing ease month after month; when the enemy entered Guan and Shaan, you made no defense at all.
translations.idiomatic: You toured south to the Huai and sea regions, stealing ease month after month. When the enemy entered Guan and Shaan, you made no defense at all.

sentences.zh: 盜賊橫潰，莫敢誰何，元元無辜，百萬塗地。

translations.literal: Bandits burst forth everywhere and none dared check them; the common people, innocent, were slaughtered by the millions across the land.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits burst forth everywhere and none dared check them. Innocent common people were slaughtered by the millions across the land.

sentences.zh: 方且製造文物，講行郊報，自謂中興。

translations.literal: Yet you were still manufacturing ritual objects, conducting suburban sacrifices, and calling it restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you were still manufacturing ritual objects, conducting suburban sacrifices, and calling it restoration.

sentences.zh: 金人乘虛直搗行在，匹馬南渡，淮甸流血。

translations.literal: The Jurchens seized the opportunity and drove straight at the traveling court; you crossed the Yangzi with a single horse, and the Huai region ran with blood.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens seized the opportunity and drove straight at the traveling court. You crossed the Yangzi with a single horse, and the Huai region ran with blood.

sentences.zh: 迨及返正寶位，移蹕建康，不為久圖，一向畏縮遠避。

translations.literal: Only when you returned to the true imperial seat and moved the court to Jiankang did you fail to plan for the long term and persistently shrink back in fear and keep your distance.
translations.idiomatic: Only when you returned to the true imperial seat and moved the court to Jiankang did you fail to plan for the long term and persistently shrink back in fear and keep your distance.

sentences.zh: 此皆失人心之大者也。

translations.literal: These are great matters in which you have lost the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: These are great matters in which you have lost the hearts of the people.

sentences.zh: 自古中興之主所以能克復舊物者，莫不本於憤恥恨怒，不能報怨，終不苟已。

translations.literal: Since antiquity, restoration emperors who were able to recover what had been lost all rooted themselves in indignation, shame, hatred, and rage, unable to avenge wrongs and never yielding until the end.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, restoration emperors who were able to recover what had been lost all rooted themselves in indignation, shame, hatred, and rage, unable to avenge wrongs and never yielding until the end.

sentences.zh: 未有乘衰微闕絕之後，固陋以為榮，苟且以為安，而能久長無禍者也。

translations.literal: Never yet has one, after inheriting a time of decline, weakness, and rupture, taken narrowness as glory and expedience as safety, and been able to endure long without calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Never yet has one, after inheriting a time of decline, weakness, and rupture, taken narrowness as glory and expedience as safety, and been able to endure long without calamity.

sentences.zh: 黃潛善與汪伯彥方以乳嫗護赤子之術待陛下，曰：「上皇之子三十人，今所存惟聖體，不可不自重愛。

translations.literal: Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan were just then treating Your Majesty with the art of a wet nurse protecting an infant, saying: "The Former Emperor had thirty sons; of those who remain today there is only Your Sacred Person—you cannot but cherish and protect yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan were just then treating Your Majesty with the art of a wet nurse protecting an infant, saying, "The Former Emperor had thirty sons; of those who remain today there is only Your Sacred Person—you cannot but cherish and protect yourself.

sentences.zh: 」曾不思宗廟則草莽湮之，陵闕則畚鍤驚之，堂堂中華戎馬生之，潛善、伯彥所以誤陛下、陷陵廟、蹙土宇、喪生靈者，可勝罪乎！

translations.literal: " They never thought that the ancestral temples were buried in wild grass, that the imperial tombs were disturbed by spades, that great China had barbarian horses trampling it—can the crimes by which Qianshan and Boyan misled Your Majesty, ruined the imperial tombs, compressed the realm, and cost countless lives be fully counted!
translations.idiomatic: " They never thought that the ancestral temples were buried in wild grass, that the imperial tombs were disturbed by spades, that great China had barbarian horses trampling it. Can the crimes by which Qianshan and Boyan misled Your Majesty, ruined the imperial tombs, compressed the realm, and cost countless lives be fully counted!

sentences.zh: 本初嗣服，既不為迎二聖之策，因循遠狩，又不為守中國之謀。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when you first succeeded to the throne, you neither adopted a plan to welcome back the Two Emperors nor, as you lingered far away on a hunting tour, devised a plan to hold China.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, when you first succeeded to the throne, you neither adopted a plan to welcome back the Two Emperors nor, as you lingered far away on a hunting tour, devised a plan to hold China.

sentences.zh: 以致於今德義不孚，號令不行，刑罰不威，爵賞不勸。

translations.literal: The result is that up to now virtue and righteousness are not trusted, orders are not obeyed, punishments inspire no awe, and ranks and rewards encourage no one.
translations.idiomatic: The result is that up to now virtue and righteousness are not trusted, orders are not obeyed, punishments inspire no awe, and ranks and rewards encourage no one.

sentences.zh: 若不更轍以救垂亡，則陛下永負孝悌之愆，常有父兄之責。

translations.literal: If you do not change course to save what is on the verge of perishing, then Your Majesty will forever bear the fault of unfiliality and constantly carry the blame of a younger brother toward his elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not change course to save what is on the verge of perishing, then Your Majesty will forever bear the fault of unfiliality and constantly carry the blame of a younger brother toward his elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 人心一去，天命難恃，雖欲羈棲山海，恐非為自全之計。

translations.literal: Once the hearts of the people are gone, the Mandate of Heaven cannot be relied upon; even if you wish to dwell in mountains and seas, I fear that will not be a plan for self-preservation.
translations.idiomatic: Once the hearts of the people are gone, the Mandate of Heaven cannot be relied upon. Even if you wish to dwell in mountains and seas, I fear that will not be a plan for self-preservation.

sentences.zh: 願下詔曰：「繼紹大統，出於臣庶之諂，而不悟其非；

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will issue an edict saying: "In succeeding to the great succession, I was moved by the flattery of officials and commoners, and did not perceive my error;
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will issue an edict saying, "In succeeding to the great succession, I was moved by the flattery of officials and commoners, and did not perceive my error;

sentences.zh: 巡狩東南，出於僥幸之心，而不虞其禍。

translations.literal: in touring southeast on a hunting progress, I was moved by a heart of lucky chance, and did not guard against the calamity that would come.
translations.idiomatic: in touring southeast on a hunting progress, I was moved by a heart of lucky chance, and did not guard against the calamity that would come.

sentences.zh: 金人逆天亂倫，朕義不共天，志思雪恥。

translations.literal: The Jurchens oppose Heaven and disorder human bonds; I, by righteousness, cannot live under the same sky with them, and my will is set on wiping away disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens oppose Heaven and disorder human bonds. I, by righteousness, cannot live under the same sky with them, and my will is set on wiping away disgrace.

sentences.zh: 父兄旅泊，陵寢荒殘，罪乃在予，無所逃責。

translations.literal: My father and elder brothers lodge as travelers; the imperial tombs lie desolate in ruin—the fault lies in me, and there is no escaping responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: My father and elder brothers lodge as travelers; the imperial tombs lie desolate in ruin—the fault lies in me, and there is no escaping responsibility.

sentences.zh: 」以此號召四海，聳動人心，決意講武，戎衣臨陣。

translations.literal: " With this summon the four seas, stir the hearts of the people, resolve to drill the army, and take the martial robe to the battlefield yourself.
translations.idiomatic: " With this summon the four seas, stir the hearts of the people, resolve to drill the army, and take the martial robe to the battlefield yourself.

sentences.zh: 按行淮、襄，收其豪英，誓以戰伐。

translations.literal: Inspect Huai and Xiang, gather their heroes and champions, and swear to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Inspect Huai and Xiang, gather their heroes and champions, and swear to fight.

sentences.zh: 天下忠義武勇，必雲合響應。

translations.literal: The loyal, righteous, brave, and martial under Heaven will surely gather like clouds and answer like echoes.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal, righteous, brave, and martial under Heaven will surely gather like clouds and answer like echoes.

sentences.zh: 陛下凡所欲為，孰不如志？

translations.literal: Whatever Your Majesty wishes to do—who will not carry it out as you desire?
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Your Majesty wishes to do—who will not carry it out as you desire?

sentences.zh: 其與退保吳、越，豈可同年而語哉！

translations.literal: How can that be spoken of in the same breath as retreating to defend Wu and Yue!
translations.idiomatic: How can that be spoken of in the same breath as retreating to defend Wu and Yue!

sentences.zh: 自古中國強盛如漢武帝、唐太宗，其得志四夷，必並吞掃滅，極其兵力而後已。

translations.literal: Since antiquity, when China was strong, as under Emperor Wu of Han and Emperor Taizong of Tang, in gaining their will over the four barbarians they always annexed, swept away, and extinguished them, exhausting military force before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, when China was strong, as under Emperor Wu of Han and Emperor Taizong of Tang, in gaining their will over the four barbarians they always annexed, swept away, and extinguished them, exhausting military force before stopping.

sentences.zh: 中國禮義所自出也，恃強淩弱且如此。

translations.literal: China is where ritual and righteousness come from; even in relying on strength to bully the weak it was thus.
translations.idiomatic: China is where ritual and righteousness come from; even in relying on strength to bully the weak it was thus.

sentences.zh: 今乃以仁慈之道、君子長者之事，望於凶頑之粘罕，豈有是理哉！

translations.literal: Now to expect from the vicious and obstinate Nijian the conduct of the humane Way and the affairs of a gentleman and elder—is there such a principle!
translations.idiomatic: Now to expect from the vicious and obstinate Nijian the conduct of the humane Way and the affairs of a gentleman and elder—is there such a principle!

sentences.zh: 今日圖復中興之策，莫大於罷絕和議，以使命之幣，為養兵之資。

translations.literal: Today's plan for restoration and revival has nothing greater than ending peace talks altogether and using the tribute sent on diplomatic missions as funds to train troops.
translations.idiomatic: Today's plan for restoration and revival has nothing greater than ending peace talks altogether and using the tribute sent on diplomatic missions as funds to train troops.

sentences.zh: 不然，則僻處東南，萬事不競。

translations.literal: Otherwise, then dwelling in a remote corner of the southeast, one competes in nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, dwelling in a remote corner of the southeast, one competes in nothing.

sentences.zh: 納賂則孰富於京室？

translations.literal: If you pay bribes, who is richer than the capital of the Jin?
translations.idiomatic: If you pay bribes, who is richer than the capital of the Jin?

sentences.zh: 納質則孰重於二聖？

translations.literal: If you send hostages, who is weightier than the Two Emperors?
translations.idiomatic: If you send hostages, who is weightier than the Two Emperors?

sentences.zh: 反復計之，所謂乞和，決無可成之理。

translations.literal: Turn it over again and again—so-called begging for peace has absolutely no principle by which it can succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Turn it over again and again—so-called begging for peace has absolutely no principle by which it can succeed.

sentences.zh: 夫大亂之後，風俗靡然，欲丕變之，在於務實效，去虛文。

translations.literal: After great disorder, custom is utterly broken down; if one wishes to change it greatly, the key lies in seeking real effect and removing empty form.
translations.idiomatic: After great disorder, custom is utterly broken down. If one wishes to change it greatly, the key lies in seeking real effect and removing empty form.

sentences.zh: 治兵擇將，誓戡大憝者，孝弟之實也；

translations.literal: Training troops and selecting generals, swearing to punish the great enemy—this is the substance of filial piety and brotherliness;
translations.idiomatic: Training troops and selecting generals, swearing to punish the great enemy—this is the substance of filial piety and brotherliness;

sentences.zh: 遣使乞和，冀幸萬一者，虛文也。

translations.literal: sending envoys to beg for peace, hoping for the one chance in ten thousand—this is empty form.
translations.idiomatic: sending envoys to beg for peace, hoping for the one chance in ten thousand—this is empty form.

sentences.zh: 屈己求賢，信用群策者，求賢之實也；

translations.literal: Humbling oneself to seek the worthy and trusting and using the counsel of many—this is the substance of seeking the worthy;
translations.idiomatic: Humbling oneself to seek the worthy and trusting and using the counsel of many—this is the substance of seeking the worthy;

sentences.zh: 外示禮貌，不用其言者，虛文也。

translations.literal: outwardly showing courtesy yet not using their words—this is empty form.
translations.idiomatic: outwardly showing courtesy yet not using their words—this is empty form.

sentences.zh: 不惟面從，必將心改，苟利於國，即日行之者，納諫之實也；

translations.literal: Not merely agreeing in face but changing in heart, and if it benefits the state carrying it out that very day—this is the substance of accepting remonstrance;
translations.idiomatic: Not merely agreeing in face but changing in heart, and if it benefits the state carrying it out that very day—this is the substance of accepting remonstrance;

sentences.zh: 和顏泛受，內惡切直者，虛文也。

translations.literal: receiving all with a pleasant countenance yet inwardly hating what is direct and upright—this is empty form.
translations.idiomatic: receiving all with a pleasant countenance yet inwardly hating what is direct and upright—this is empty form.

sentences.zh: 擢智勇忠直之人，待禦以恩威，結約以誠信者，任將之實也；

translations.literal: Promoting men of wisdom, courage, loyalty, and uprightness, treating generals with both favor and awe, and binding them by covenant in good faith—this is the substance of employing generals;
translations.idiomatic: Promoting men of wisdom, courage, loyalty, and uprightness, treating generals with both favor and awe, and binding them by covenant in good faith—this is the substance of employing generals;

sentences.zh: 親厚庸奴，等威不立者，虛文也。

translations.literal: being close and thick with mediocre subordinates, not establishing equal authority—this is empty form.
translations.idiomatic: favoring worthless underlings and failing to uphold proper rank—this is mere show.

sentences.zh: 汰疲弱，擇壯勇，足其衣食，申明階級，以變其驕悍之習者，治軍之實也；

translations.literal: weeding out the weak and feeble, selecting the strong and brave, providing fully for their clothing and food, clarifying ranks and grades, to change their proud and fierce habits—this is the substance of governing the army;
translations.idiomatic: Culling the weak, choosing the stalwart, supplying their needs, enforcing clear hierarchy, and breaking their arrogant, violent ways—this is how an army is truly governed;

sentences.zh: 教習兒戲，紀律蕩然者，虛文也。

translations.literal: drilling them in childish play, discipline utterly dissolved—this is empty form.
translations.idiomatic: training soldiers as though at play while discipline collapses—this is mere show.

sentences.zh: 遴選守刺，久於其官，痛刈奸贓，廣行寬恤者，愛民之實也；

translations.literal: carefully selecting prefects and regional inspectors, keeping them long in their posts, sternly cutting out the corrupt and embezzling, broadly practicing clemency and relief—this is the substance of loving the people;
translations.idiomatic: Choosing magistrates with care, leaving them in office long enough to govern, rooting out graft without mercy, and extending mercy widely—this is how a ruler truly loves his people;

sentences.zh: 軍須戎具，征求取辦，蠲租赦令，苟以欺之者，虛文也。

translations.literal: military supplies and weapons, requisitioning to fulfill quotas, rent remissions and amnesty edicts—all done perfunctorily to deceive—this is empty form.
translations.idiomatic: requisitioning arms and provisions on demand, issuing tax remissions and amnesties only to placate—this is mere show.

sentences.zh: 若夫保宗廟、陵寢、土地、人民，以此六實者行乎其間，則為中興之實政也。

translations.literal: if one preserves the ancestral temple, imperial tombs, territory, and people, and lets these six substances operate among them, then this is the true policy of revival.
translations.idiomatic: If the ancestral temple, imperial tombs, land, and people are preserved, and these six real measures are put into practice, then this is a genuine policy of national revival.

sentences.zh: 陵廟荒圮，土宇日蹙，衣冠黔首，為血為肉，以此六虛者行乎其間，則為今日虛文。

translations.literal: imperial tombs and temples lie in ruin, territory shrinks daily, caps and gowns and black-headed commoners become blood and flesh, and these six empty forms operate among them—this is today's empty show.
translations.idiomatic: Tombs and temples crumble, the realm contracts day by day, and scholar and commoner alike are butchered—while these six hollow gestures go on. That is the empty pageantry of our age.

sentences.zh: 陛下戴黃屋，建幄殿，質明輦出房，雉扇金爐夾侍兩陛，仗馬衛兵儼分儀式，讚者引百官入奉起居，以此度日。

translations.literal: Your Majesty wears the yellow canopy, holds court in the curtained hall, at dawn the palanquin leaves the inner chambers, feathered fans and golden censers attend on both sides of the throne, ceremonial horses and guards stand in strict formation, announcers lead the hundred officials in to inquire after Your Majesty's health—thus passing the days.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty dons the imperial canopy, sits in the curtained hall, and at dawn rides out from the inner palace. Feathered fans and golden censers flank the throne; ceremonial horses and guards array themselves in order; heralds lead the officials forward to pay their respects—and so the days pass.

sentences.zh: 彼粘罕者，晝夜厲兵，跨河越岱，電掃中土，遂有吞吸江湖，蹂踐衡霍之意。

translations.literal: That Nijian night and day sharpens his arms, crosses the Yellow River and Mount Tai, sweeps the Central Plain like lightning, and now intends to swallow rivers and lakes and trample Heng and Huo.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Nijian drills his troops day and night, crosses the Yellow River and Mount Tai, and sweeps the heartland like lightning—intent on swallowing the Yangtze basin and trampling the sacred mountains of Heng and Huo.

sentences.zh: 吾方擁虛器，茫然未知所之。

translations.literal: We on our side hold empty vessels, dazed, not knowing where we are going.
translations.idiomatic: We cling to hollow symbols of power, adrift and without direction.

sentences.zh: 君子小人，勢不兩立。

translations.literal: Gentlemen and petty men—their positions cannot coexist.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman and the petty man cannot stand together.

sentences.zh: 仁宗皇帝在位，得君子最多。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong was on the throne, he obtained the most gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Renzong, more true gentlemen entered service than at any other time.

sentences.zh: 小人亦時見用，然罪者則斥；

translations.literal: Petty men were also sometimes employed, yet those guilty were dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: Petty men were sometimes used, but the guilty were cast out;

sentences.zh: 君子亦或見廢，然忠顯則收。

translations.literal: Gentlemen were also sometimes removed, yet those loyal and eminent were recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen were sometimes pushed aside, but the loyal and worthy were brought back.

sentences.zh: 故其成當世之功，貽後人之輔者，皆君子也。

translations.literal: Therefore those who achieved the merit of their age and bequeathed aid to posterity were all gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Thus every man who built the achievements of that age and left strength for later generations was a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 至王安石則不然，斥絕君子，一去而不還；

translations.literal: When it came to Wang Anshi it was not so—he rejected gentlemen utterly, and once gone they never returned;
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Anshi it was otherwise: he drove the gentlemen away, and once gone they never came back;

sentences.zh: 崇信小人，一任則不改。

translations.literal: He venerated and trusted petty men, and once given office they were never changed.
translations.idiomatic: He exalted petty men and, once entrusted with power, never replaced them.

sentences.zh: 故其敗當時之政，為後世之害者，皆小人也。

translations.literal: Therefore those who ruined the policies of the time and became harms to posterity were all petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Thus every man who wrecked the governance of that age and poisoned later times was a petty man.

sentences.zh: 仁宗皇帝所養之君子，既日遠而銷亡矣。

translations.literal: The gentlemen whom Emperor Renzong cultivated have already grown daily more distant and vanished away.
translations.idiomatic: The gentlemen Renzong had nurtured are now far gone, fading day by day.

sentences.zh: 安石所致之小人，方蕃息而未艾也。

translations.literal: The petty men whom Anshi brought forth are just now multiplying and have not yet ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The petty men Anshi set loose are still breeding and have not yet spent their force.

sentences.zh: 所以誤國破家，至毒至烈，以致二聖屈辱，羿、莽擅朝，伏節死難者不過一二人。

translations.literal: Hence they misled the state and ruined families, to a poison and violence most extreme, so that the Two Emperors suffered humiliation, Yi and Mang usurped the court, and those who held to integrity and died in the calamity were no more than one or two.
translations.idiomatic: They misled the realm and shattered households with the bitterest poison, until the Two Emperors were humiliated, usurpers seized the court like Yi and Wang Mang, and scarcely one or two men died holding fast to their integrity.

sentences.zh: 此浮華輕薄之害，明主之所畏而深戒者也。

translations.literal: This is the harm of flashy, frivolous conduct—what an enlightened ruler fears and deeply warns against.
translations.idiomatic: This is the damage done by showy, shallow men—the very thing a wise ruler dreads and guards against.

sentences.zh: 古之稱中興者曰：「撥亂世，反之正。

translations.literal: The ancients spoke of revival, saying: "Set a chaotic age aright and return it to the proper way.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients defined revival thus: "In a chaotic age, set things aright and restore the proper order.

sentences.zh: 」今之亂亦云甚矣，其反正而興之，在陛下；

translations.literal: " The disorder of today is also said to be extreme; whether to set it aright and revive it lies with Your Majesty;
translations.idiomatic: " Today's disorder is no less severe. Whether the realm is set aright and revived depends on Your Majesty;

sentences.zh: 其遂陵遲不振，亦在陛下。

translations.literal: Whether it continues to decline and fail to recover also lies with Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Whether it keeps sinking and never rises again also depends on Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 昔宗澤一老從官耳，猶能推誠感動群賊，北連懷、衛，同迎二聖，克期密應者，無慮數十萬人。

translations.literal: Formerly Zong Ze was only an old attendant official, yet he could move bandit groups through sincerity, link north with Huai and Wei, jointly welcome the Two Emperors, and those who agreed on a set date to respond in secret numbered, without exaggeration, several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zong Ze was no more than an elderly attendant in office, yet by sincerity he moved whole bands of rebels; north through Huai and Wei men pledged together to welcome the Two Emperors, and those who secretly agreed to answer on a fixed day numbered, at the least, several hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 何況陛下身為子弟，欲北向而有為，將見舉四海為陛下用，期以十年，必能掃除妖沴，遠迓父兄，稱宋中興。

translations.literal: How much more so Your Majesty, as a son and brother, wishing to face north and act—you will see all within the four seas rise for Your Majesty's use; within ten years you will surely sweep away evil portents, welcome back your father and elder brother from afar, and be hailed as the revival of Song.
translations.idiomatic: How much more, then, when Your Majesty—son and brother to the captive emperors—turns north with purpose! All under Heaven will rally to you; in ten years you can drive off calamity, bring home your father and elder brother, and win the name of Song's revival.

sentences.zh: 其與惕息遁藏，蹈危負恥如今日，豈不天地相絕哉！

translations.literal: How can that be spoken of in the same breath as cowering in fear, hiding away, treading danger and bearing shame as today—is this not Heaven and Earth turned against each other!
translations.idiomatic: How can that be compared with cowering in dread, hiding in shame, and living as we do today in peril and disgrace—as though Heaven and Earth themselves were torn apart!

sentences.zh: 疏入，宰相呂頤浩惡其切直，除直龍圖閣、主管江州太平觀。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the chief councilor Lü Yihao resented its blunt directness and appointed him Directly Attached to the Hall of Dragon Images, Supervisor of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the memorial entered court, Chief Councilor Lü Yihao, angered by its bluntness, had him appointed Directly Attached to the Hall of Dragon Images and put in charge of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，詔內外官各言省費、裕國、強兵、息民之策，寅以十事應詔，曰修政事、備邊陲、治軍旅、用人才、除盜賊、信賞罰、理財用、核名實、屏諛佞、去奸慝。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year, an edict ordered officials within and without to speak on policies for economizing expenditure, enriching the state, strengthening the army, and giving the people rest. Yin responded to the decree with ten matters, namely: repair government affairs, prepare the borderlands, govern the armies, employ men of talent, eliminate bandits and robbers, uphold rewards and punishments, manage finances, verify names against reality, remove flattery and sycophancy, and banish the wicked and vicious.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year, an edict called on all officials to propose ways to cut costs, enrich the state, strengthen the army, and give the people rest. Yin answered with ten measures: reform administration, secure the frontiers, discipline the armies, employ talent, suppress banditry, enforce reward and punishment, manage revenue, match names to reality, drive out flatterers, and remove the wicked.

sentences.zh: 疏上不報，尋命知永州。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and received no response; soon he was appointed prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went unanswered; soon afterward he was made prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興四年十二月，復召為起居郎，遷中書舍人，賜三品服。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Shaoxing, he was again summoned as Recorder of the Emperor's Actions, transferred to Drafting Attendant in the Central Secretariat, and granted third-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Shaoxing 4 he was recalled as Recorder of the Emperor's Actions, promoted to Drafting Attendant in the Central Secretariat, and granted robes of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 時議遣使入雲中，寅上疏言：

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of sending envoys into Yunzhong; Yin submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court debated sending envoys into Yunzhong. Yin submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 女真驚動陵寢，殘毀宗廟，劫質二聖，乃吾國之大仇也。

translations.literal: The Jurchen disturbed the imperial tombs, ravaged the ancestral temple, and took the Two Emperors hostage—this is the great enemy of our state.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen violated the imperial tombs, destroyed the ancestral temple, and seized the Two Emperors as hostages—they are the great enemy of our state.

sentences.zh: 頃者，誤國之臣遣使求和，以苟歲月，九年於茲，其效如何？

translations.literal: Recently, ministers who misled the state sent envoys seeking peace to scrape through month by month—it is now nine years—what has been the effect?
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago, the ministers who ruined the state sent envoys to sue for peace, buying time month by month. Nine years have passed—what has it accomplished?

sentences.zh: 幸陛下灼見邪言，漸圖恢復，忠臣義士聞風興起，各思自效。

translations.literal: Fortunately Your Majesty clearly saw perverse words and gradually planned recovery; loyal ministers and men of righteousness, hearing the wind, rose up, each thinking to devote himself.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, thank Heaven, saw through those false counsels and began to plan recovery; loyal and righteous men everywhere took heart and sought to serve.

sentences.zh: 今無故蹈庸臣之轍，忘復仇之義，陳自辱之辭，臣切為陛下不取也。

translations.literal: Now for no reason to tread the track of mediocre ministers, forget the duty of revenge, and offer words of self-humiliation—I deeply hold that Your Majesty ought not take this course.
translations.idiomatic: Now, for no reason, to follow mediocre ministers again, forget the duty of vengeance, and offer self-abasing words—I cannot believe Your Majesty would choose this.

sentences.zh: 若謂不少貶屈，如二聖何？

translations.literal: If one says that without some humiliation and abasement, what of the Two Emperors?
translations.idiomatic: If the objection is that without some humbling of ourselves, what becomes of the Two Emperors?

sentences.zh: 則自丁未以至甲寅，所為卑辭厚禮以問安迎請為名而遣使者，不知幾人矣，知二聖之所在者誰歟？

translations.literal: Then from dingwei to jiayin, those sent as envoys under the name of humble words and lavish gifts to inquire after health and request their return—who knows how many—yet who knows where the Two Emperors are?
translations.idiomatic: From dingwei through jiayin, how many envoys went forth with humble words and rich gifts, claiming to inquire after the emperors and beg their return? Yet who knows where the Two Emperors are?

sentences.zh: 聞二聖之聲音者誰歟？

translations.literal: Who has heard the voices of the Two Emperors?
translations.idiomatic: Who has heard their voices?

sentences.zh: 得女真之要領而息兵者誰歟？

translations.literal: Who has grasped the Jurchen's vital point and halted the war?
translations.idiomatic: Who has seized the Jurchen by the throat and stopped the fighting?

sentences.zh: 臣但見丙午而後，通和之使歸未息肩，而黃河、長淮、大江相繼失險矣。

translations.literal: Your subject has only seen that after bingwu, peace envoys returned with shoulders still unrelaxed, while the Yellow River, the Huai, and the great Yangzi successively lost their strategic defenses.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen only this: since bingwu, envoys of peace return exhausted, while the Yellow River, the Huai, and the Yangtze have fallen one after another.

sentences.zh: 夫女真知中國所重在二聖，所懼在劫質，所畏在用兵，而中國坐受此餌，既久而不悟也。

translations.literal: The Jurchen knows that China values the Two Emperors above all, fears hostage-taking, and dreads the use of arms—yet China has sat still taking this bait, long without waking to it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen know that we prize the Two Emperors above all, dread hostage-taking, and fear war—yet we have swallowed their bait for years without waking.

sentences.zh: 天下謂自是必改圖矣，何為復出此謬計邪？

translations.literal: All under Heaven thought that from then on the plan would surely change—why bring forth this absurd scheme again?
translations.idiomatic: The realm believed the policy would change at last—why revive this foolish plan?

sentences.zh: 當今之事，莫大於金人之怨。

translations.literal: Of affairs today, nothing is greater than enmity with the Jin people.
translations.idiomatic: Of all matters today, none is greater than hatred of the Jin.

sentences.zh: 欲報此怨，必殄此仇。

translations.literal: To repay this enmity, one must exterminate this foe.
translations.idiomatic: To settle this grievance, the enemy must be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 用復仇之議，而不用講和之政，使天下皆知女真為不共戴天之仇，人人有致死之心，然後二聖之怨可平，陛下人子之職舉矣。

translations.literal: Adopt the policy of revenge and not the policy of peace talks; let all under Heaven know the Jurchen as an enemy with whom one cannot share the sky, so that every man has a heart to die for the cause—then the grievance of the Two Emperors can be settled and Your Majesty's duty as a son fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Choose the path of vengeance, not negotiation. Let every man under Heaven know the Jurchen as an enemy he cannot live under the same sky with, until all are ready to die for the cause—then the Two Emperors' wrong may be redressed and Your Majesty's filial duty fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 苟為不然，彼或願與陛下歃盟泗水之上，不知何以待之？

translations.literal: If it is otherwise, they may wish to swear alliance with Your Majesty by the Si River—how would one receive that?
translations.idiomatic: If not, they may offer to swear brotherhood with Your Majesty beside the Si River—how then should you answer?

sentences.zh: 望聖意直以世仇無可通之義，寢罷使命。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty's sacred intent will take them as hereditary foes with whom there is no basis for communication, and put to rest and abolish these missions.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will treat them as hereditary enemies with whom no dealings are possible, and put an end to these embassies altogether.

sentences.zh: 高宗嘉納，云：「胡寅論使事，詞旨剴切，深得獻納論思之體。

translations.literal: Gaozong praised and accepted it, saying: "Hu Yin's discussion of the envoy question, in wording and intent, is incisive and cutting; it fully accords with the proper form of offering counsel for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong approved the memorial, saying: "Hu Yin's words on the envoy question are sharp and to the point; they embody the spirit in which a subject should offer counsel for the throne's deliberation.

sentences.zh: 」召至都堂諭旨，仍降詔獎諭。

translations.literal: " He was summoned to the Chief Council Chamber to receive the imperial message, and an edict of commendation was also issued.
translations.idiomatic: " He was called to the Chief Council Chamber to hear the imperial response, and an edict of praise was issued besides.

sentences.zh: 既而右僕射張浚自江上還，奏遣使為兵家機權，竟反前旨。

translations.literal: Subsequently the Right Vice Director Zhang Jun returned from the river front and memorialized that sending envoys was a military stratagem, and in the end reversed the previous intent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Right Vice Director Zhang Jun returned from the front and argued that sending envoys was a military expedient; in the end the earlier decision was reversed.

sentences.zh: 寅復奏疏言：「今日大計，隻合明復仇之義，用賢修德，息兵訓民，以圖北向。

translations.literal: Yin again submitted a memorial, saying: "Today's great plan ought solely to proclaim clearly the principle of revenge, employ the worthy and cultivate virtue, give the army rest and train the people, in order to plan facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Yin submitted another memorial: "The great plan for today is to proclaim vengeance openly, employ the worthy and cultivate virtue, rest the armies and train the people, and prepare to turn north.

sentences.zh: 倘或未可，則堅守待時。

translations.literal: If that is not yet possible, then hold firm and await the time.
translations.idiomatic: If the time is not ripe, then hold fast and wait.

sentences.zh: 若夫二三其德，無一定之論，必不能有所立。

translations.literal: If one wavers in virtue and has no fixed doctrine, one can surely accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: But to shift one's stand and hold no firm view is to accomplish nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 」寅既與浚異，遂乞便郡就養。

translations.literal: " Yin, having differed with Zhang Jun, then requested an easy prefecture in which to retire and care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: " Having broken with Zhang Jun, Yin asked for a comfortable post nearby so he could retire and support his parents.

sentences.zh: 始，寅上言：「近年書命多出詞臣好惡之私，使人主命德討罪之詞，未免玩人喪德之失，乞命詞臣以飾情相悅、含怒相訾為戒。

translations.literal: Earlier Yin had submitted: "In recent years edicts and commands often issued from the private likes and dislikes of drafting officials, so that orders from the sovereign commanding virtue and condemning wrong could not avoid the fault of treating people lightly and losing virtue. I ask that drafting officials be commanded to take as their warning flattering with insincere feeling and reproaching with hidden anger.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yin had said: "In recent years many edicts have reflected the private likes and dislikes of the drafting officials, so that the sovereign's words of moral command and condemnation have often become mere playthings that erode virtue. I ask that the drafters be warned against smoothing feelings with false courtesy and venting anger in veiled reproach.

sentences.zh: 」故寅所撰詞多誥誡，於是忌嫉者眾。

translations.literal: " Therefore the drafts Yin composed were mostly admonitions—and so those who envied and hated him were many.
translations.idiomatic: " For this reason Yin's drafts were mostly admonitory, and many came to resent him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷辨宣仁聖烈之誣，行遣章惇、蔡卞，皆宰臣面授上旨，令寅撰進。

translations.literal: When the court cleared the slanders against Empress Xuanren the Sage and Formidable, and issued edicts banishing Zhang Dun and Cai Bian—all these were orders the chief ministers received face to face from the emperor, directing Yin to draft and submit them.
translations.idiomatic: When the court cleared the calumnies against Empress Xuanren and issued edicts banishing Zhang Dun and Cai Bian, the chief ministers received the emperor's instructions in person and had Yin draft the documents.

sentences.zh: 除徽猷閣待制、知邵州，辭。

translations.literal: He was appointed Awaiting Orders at the Hall of Imperial Exemplars and made prefect of Shaozhou; he declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Awaiting Orders at the Hall of Imperial Exemplars and prefect of Shaozhou, but declined.

sentences.zh: 改集英殿修撰，復以待制改知嚴州，又改知永州。

translations.literal: He was changed to Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Eminence, again as Awaiting Orders made prefect of Yanzhou, then again changed to prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Eminence, then made Awaiting Orders and prefect of Yanzhou, and later transferred to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗皇帝、寧德皇后訃至，朝廷用故事以日易月，寅上疏言：「禮：仇不復則服不除。

translations.literal: When the death announcements of Emperor Huizong and Empress Cide arrived, the court followed precedent in substituting days for months; Yin submitted a memorial, saying: "According to ritual: if the enemy is not avenged, mourning garments are not removed.
translations.idiomatic: When word came of the deaths of Emperor Huizong and Empress Cide, the court followed precedent and shortened the mourning period. Yin submitted a memorial: "Ritual teaches: if the enemy is not avenged, mourning clothes are not laid aside.

sentences.zh: 願降詔旨，用喪三年，衣墨臨戎，以化天下。

translations.literal: I hope an edict will be issued adopting the three-year mourning, wearing black while facing war, to transform all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty decree full three-year mourning, take the field in black, and thereby transform the realm.

sentences.zh: 」尋除禮部侍郎、兼侍講兼直學士院。

translations.literal: " Soon he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently Lecturer and Academician of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward he was made Vice Minister of Rites, Lecturer, and Academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，免喪，時秦檜當國，除徽猷閣直學士、提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he entered mourning; after the mourning period, when Qin Hui held power, he was appointed Direct Academician of the Hall of Imperial Exemplars and promoted to oversee the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he observed mourning; when mourning ended and Qin Hui dominated the court, he was made Direct Academician of the Hall of Imperial Exemplars and put in charge of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄乞致仕，遂歸衡州。

translations.literal: Soon he requested retirement and returned to Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he asked to retire and went home to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 檜既忌寅，雖告老，猶憤之，坐與李光書譏訕朝政落職。

translations.literal: Qin Hui had long envied Yin; though Yin had reported himself old, Qin still harbored anger, and Yin was demoted on account of letters with Li Guang ridiculing court policy.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui had long resented Yin; though Yin had retired, Qin still pursued him, and Yin was stripped of rank for letters exchanged with Li Guang that mocked court policy.

sentences.zh: 右正言章復劾寅不持本生母服不孝，諫通鄰好不忠，責授果州團練副使、新州安置。

translations.literal: The Right Remonstrator Zhang Fu impeached Yin for not observing mourning for his birth mother—as unfilial—and for remonstrating against good relations with neighbors—as disloyal; he was demoted to Vice Militia Commissioner of Guozhou and assigned to Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrator Zhang Fu accused Yin of failing to mourn his biological mother—charging unfiliality—and of opposing friendly relations with neighboring states—charging disloyalty. Yin was demoted to Vice Militia Commissioner of Guozhou and exiled to Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 檜死，詔自便，尋復其官。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui died, an edict allowed him to go where he pleased; soon his offices were restored.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin Hui's death an edict freed him to live where he chose, and soon his rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十一年卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: He died in the twenty-first year of Shaoxing, at age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shaoxing 21, aged fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 寅志節豪邁，初擢第，中書侍郎張邦昌欲以女妻之，不許。

translations.literal: Yin's aspiration and integrity were bold and lofty. When he first passed the examinations, the Vice Director of the Central Secretariat Zhang Bangchang wished to give him his daughter in marriage; he refused.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was a man of fierce integrity. When he first passed the examinations, Vice Director Zhang Bangchang of the Central Secretariat offered him his daughter in marriage; he refused.

sentences.zh: 始，安國頗重秦檜之大節，及檜擅國，寅遂與之絕。

translations.literal: At first Anguo held Qin Hui's great integrity in high regard; once Qin monopolized the state, Yin broke with him altogether.
translations.idiomatic: At first Hu Anguo greatly respected Qin Hui's public integrity; once Qin seized control of the state, Yin broke with him completely.

sentences.zh: 新州謫命下，即日就道。

translations.literal: When the order of exile to Xinzhou was issued, he set out that very day.
translations.idiomatic: When the order banishing him to Xinzhou arrived, he left the same day.

sentences.zh: 在謫所著《讀史管見》數十萬言，及《論語詳說》，皆行於世。

translations.literal: While in exile he wrote "Glimpses from Reading History" in several hundred thousand words, and "Detailed Expositions on the Analects"—both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: In exile he wrote "Glimpses from Reading History," several hundred thousand words long, and "Detailed Expositions on the Analects"; both works circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 其為文根著義理，有《斐然集》三十卷。

translations.literal: His writings were rooted in principle; he had the "Feiran Collection" in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was grounded in moral principle. His "Feiran Collection" ran to thirty scrolls.

translations.literal: 〈Sons〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Sons〉

sentences.zh: 宏

translations.literal: Hong
translations.idiomatic: Hong

sentences.zh: 宏字仁仲，幼事楊時、侯仲良，而卒傳其父之學。

translations.literal: Hong, styled Renzhong, in youth studied under Yang Shi and Hou Zhongliang, and in the end transmitted his father's learning.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, styled Renzhong, studied in youth under Yang Shi and Hou Zhongliang, and in the end carried on his father's doctrine.

sentences.zh: 優遊衡山下餘二十年，玩心神明，不舍晝夜。

translations.literal: At leisure beneath Mount Heng for more than twenty years, he cultivated the spirit and clarity, never resting day or night.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years he lived at ease beneath Mount Heng, refining his inner spirit without ceasing, day or night.

sentences.zh: 張栻師事之。

translations.literal: Zhang Shi took him as master.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi studied under him as his disciple.

sentences.zh: 紹興間上書，其略曰：

translations.literal: During the Shaoxing era he submitted a memorial; its gist said:
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaoxing period he submitted a memorial, which in summary said:

sentences.zh: 治天下有本，仁也。

translations.literal: Governing all under Heaven has a root, and that is benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: To govern the realm has a foundation, and that foundation is benevolence.

sentences.zh: 何謂仁？

translations.literal: What is benevolence?
translations.idiomatic: What is benevolence?

sentences.zh: 心也。

translations.literal: The heart.
translations.idiomatic: The heart.

sentences.zh: 心官茫茫，莫知其鄉，若為知其體乎？

translations.literal: The heart's office is vast and dim; no one knows its native place—how then may one know its substance?
translations.idiomatic: The heart is boundless and obscure; none can say where it dwells—how then can one grasp its nature?

sentences.zh: 有所不察則不知矣。

translations.literal: Where there is failure to examine, there is no knowing.
translations.idiomatic: Fail to examine it, and you cannot know it.

sentences.zh: 有所顧慮，有所畏懼，則雖有能知能察之良心，亦浸消亡而不自知，此臣之所大憂也。

translations.literal: When there is calculation and fear, then even though one has the innate heart that can know and examine, it is gradually extinguished without one's knowing—this is what your subject greatly fears.
translations.idiomatic: When calculation and fear take hold, the innate heart that can know and discern withers away unnoticed—even though it is still there. This is what I fear most.

sentences.zh: 夫敵國據形勝之地，逆臣僭位於中原，牧馬駸駸，欲爭天下。

translations.literal: The enemy state holds terrain of strategic advantage; a rebellious minister usurps position in the Central Plain; horses graze in growing numbers—they wish to contend for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy holds the commanding ground; a rebel sits in usurpation at the heart of the realm; their horses graze ever closer—they mean to wrest the empire from us.

sentences.zh: 臣不是懼，而以良心為大憂者，蓋良心充於一身，通於天地，宰制萬事，統攝億兆之本也。

translations.literal: Your subject is not afraid of these; yet taking the innate heart as the great concern is because the innate heart fills the person, communicates with Heaven and Earth, governs the ten thousand affairs, and is the root that commands the hundred million.
translations.idiomatic: I do not say these things because I fear the enemy. I speak of the innate heart because it fills the self, reaches through Heaven and Earth, governs all affairs, and is the root from which the multitude are ruled.

sentences.zh: 察天理莫如屏欲，存良心莫如立志。

translations.literal: To discern Heaven's principle nothing surpasses screening out desire; to preserve the innate heart nothing surpasses establishing purpose.
translations.idiomatic: To see Heaven's principle, nothing helps more than restraining desire; to keep the innate heart alive, nothing helps more than setting one's will.

sentences.zh: 陛下亦有朝廷政事不幹於慮，便嬖智巧不陳於前，妃嬪佳麗不幸於左右時矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty also has times when court affairs do not reach your deliberation, when clever favorites are not set before you, and when consorts and beauties are not constantly at your side.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty too has moments when state affairs never reach your thoughts, when clever favorites stand far off, and when consorts and beauties are absent from your side.

sentences.zh: 陛下試於此時沉思靜慮，方今之世，當陛下之身，事孰為大乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, try at such a moment to think deeply and reflect quietly: in the world today, in Your Majesty's own person—what matter is greatest?
translations.idiomatic: At such a moment, I ask Your Majesty to think deeply and in silence: in this age, in your own person—what matter is greatest?

sentences.zh: 孰為急乎？

translations.literal: What is most urgent?
translations.idiomatic: What is most urgent?

sentences.zh: 必有歉然而餒，惻然而痛，坐起彷徨不能自安者，則良心可察，而臣言可信矣。

translations.literal: Surely there will be shame and emptiness, compassion and pain, and unrest sitting and rising—you cannot be at ease—then the innate heart can be examined, and your subject's words trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Surely shame will come, and hollowness; compassion will ache in you; you will rise and sit unable to rest. Then the innate heart may be known—and my words believed.

sentences.zh: 昔舜以匹夫為天子，瞽叟以匹夫為天子父，受天下之養，豈不足於窮約哉？

translations.literal: Formerly Shun was emperor though a common man, and Gousou was the emperor's father though a common man; he received the nourishment of all under Heaven—was he not beyond want and deprivation?
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Shun became emperor though he was a common man, and Gousou became the father of an emperor though he was a common man. He received the sustenance of the realm—was he still in want?

sentences.zh: 而瞽叟猶不悅。

translations.literal: Yet Gousou was still not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gousou was not content.

sentences.zh: 自常情觀之，舜可以免矣，而舜蹙然有憂之，舉天下之大無足以解憂者。

translations.literal: From ordinary sentiment one might say Shun could have absolved himself, yet Shun knit his brow in worry, and nothing under all Heaven was great enough to dissolve his grief.
translations.idiomatic: By ordinary feeling one might say Shun had done enough, yet Shun furrowed his brow in grief, and nothing in all the world could ease it.

sentences.zh: 徽宗皇帝身享天下之奉幾三十年。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong personally enjoyed the tribute of all under Heaven for nearly thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong enjoyed the empire's bounty for nearly thirty years.

sentences.zh: 欽宗皇帝生於深宮，享乘輿之次，以至為帝。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong was born in the deep palace, enjoyed the rank of the imperial carriage, and came at last to be emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong was born in the inner palace, raised to imperial rank, and at last ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 一旦劫於仇敵，遠適窮荒，衣裘失司服之制，飲食失膳夫之味，居處失宮殿之安、妃嬪之好，動無威嚴，辛苦墊隘。

translations.literal: In a single day they were seized by the enemy, driven far to a desolate wilderness; robes lost the regulation of the Director of Robes, food lost the savor of the imperial kitchen, dwelling lost the ease of palaces and the pleasure of consorts; in movement they had no dignity—hardship and cramped misery.
translations.idiomatic: Then in a single day they were taken by the enemy and cast into distant wasteland. Their robes no longer followed court ritual; their food no longer tasted of the imperial kitchen; their dwellings no longer knew palace ease or the company of consorts. Stripped of majesty, they endured hardship and confinement.

sentences.zh: 其願陛下加兵敵國，心目睽睽，猶饑渴之於飲食。

translations.literal: Their wish that Your Majesty would increase troops against the enemy state — their eyes stare fixed and wide, like hunger and thirst toward food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: They long for Your Majesty to send armies against the enemy; their eyes strain in fixed hope, as hunger and thirst crave food and drink.

sentences.zh: 庶幾一得生還，父子兄弟相持而泣，歡若平生。

translations.literal: Perhaps if they could once return alive, father and sons and brothers would embrace and weep, rejoicing as in former days.
translations.idiomatic: If only they might once come home alive — fathers and sons, brothers clasping one another in tears, joy like that of years past.

sentences.zh: 引領東望，九年於此矣。

translations.literal: Craning their necks they gaze east; nine years have passed in this state.
translations.idiomatic: Necks craned eastward — nine years have passed thus.

sentences.zh: 夫以疏賤，念此痛心，當食則嗌，未嘗不投箸而起，思欲有為，況陛下當其任乎？

translations.literal: As one remote and lowly, thinking of this pains the heart; at meals I choke, never failing to cast down chopsticks and rise, thinking to act — how much the more for Your Majesty, who holds the charge?
translations.idiomatic: Remote and lowly though I am, the thought wrings my heart: at every meal I choke, always casting down my chopsticks to rise, hungering to act — and how much more should Your Majesty, who bears the office?

sentences.zh: 而在廷之臣，不能對揚天心，充陛下仁孝之志，反以天子之尊，北面仇敵。

translations.literal: Yet the ministers at court cannot respond to Heaven's intent and fulfill Your Majesty's benevolent and filial resolve; instead, with the Son of Heaven's dignity, they face north toward the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ministers in court cannot echo Heaven's will or fulfill Your Majesty's benevolent and filial purpose; they use the Son of Heaven's own dignity to bow north to the foe.

sentences.zh: 陛下自念，以此事親，於舜何如也？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, reflect: to serve your parents in this way — how does it compare with Shun?
translations.idiomatic: Consider, Your Majesty: to serve your parents thus — how would Shun have judged it?

sentences.zh: 且群臣智謀淺短，自度不足以任大事，故欲偷安江左，貪圖寵榮，皆為身謀爾。

translations.literal: Moreover, the ministers' wisdom and stratagems are shallow and short; measuring themselves as unequal to great affairs, they wish to steal ease south of the Yangtze, greedily seek favor and glory — all schemes for themselves alone.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the ministers' counsel is shallow and small; knowing themselves unequal to great undertakings, they seek ease south of the Yangtze and grasp at favor and rank — every move is for themselves.

sentences.zh: 陛下乃信之，以為必持是可以進撫中原，展省陵廟，來歸兩宮，亦何誤耶！

translations.literal: Your Majesty nevertheless trusts them, thinking that surely holding to this can advance to pacify the Central Plain, visit imperial tombs and temples, and bring back the Two Palaces — what an error!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty still trusts them, believing this course will surely restore the Central Plain, allow visits to the imperial tombs, and bring home the Two Palaces — what a grievous mistake!

sentences.zh: 萬世不磨之辱，臣子必報之仇，子孫之所以寢苫枕戈，弗與共天下者也；

translations.literal: A shame that ten thousand generations cannot erase, a feud that ministers and sons must surely avenge — the reason descendants sleep on brushwood and pillow on weapons, refusing to share the realm with them;
translations.idiomatic: An indelible shame for ten thousand generations, a feud ministers and sons must avenge — the reason posterity sleeps on brushwood and keeps a spear at the pillow, unwilling to share the realm with them;

sentences.zh: 而陛下顧慮畏懼，忘之不敢以為仇。

translations.literal: yet Your Majesty, anxious and fearful, forgets it and dares not treat it as a feud.
translations.idiomatic: yet Your Majesty, in anxious fear, sets it aside and dares not call it a feud.
