sentences.zh: 臣下僭逆，有明目張膽顯為負叛者，有協讚亂賊為之羽翰者，有依隨兩端欲以中立自免者，而陛下顧慮畏懼，寬之不敢以為討。

translations.literal: Among subordinates there are usurpers and traitors: some openly and brazenly show themselves rebels; some assist and praise rebel brigands as wings and helpers; some follow both sides, seeking neutrality to save themselves — yet Your Majesty, anxious and fearful, is lenient and dares not punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Among your subjects are usurpers and turncoats: some openly rebel; some lend wings to rebels; some fence-sit, hoping neutrality will save them — yet Your Majesty, full of anxious fear, pardons them and dares not punish.

sentences.zh: 守此不改，是祖宗之靈，終天暴露，無與復存也；

translations.literal: If this is held unchanged, then the spirits of the ancestors, exposed under Heaven to the end, will have none to restore them;
translations.idiomatic: Hold to this, and the spirits of our ancestors remain exposed under Heaven, with none left to restore them;

sentences.zh: 父兄之身，終天困辱，而求歸之望絕也；

translations.literal: the persons of father and elder brothers, humiliated to the end of their days, and the hope of return cut off;
translations.idiomatic: father and elder brothers suffer humiliation to their last day, and all hope of return is lost;

sentences.zh: 中原士民，沒身塗炭，無所赴訴也。

translations.literal: the scholars and people of the Central Plain, submerged in calamity to their deaths, with nowhere to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: the scholars and common people of the Central Plain sink into misery unto death, with no place to cry for help.

sentences.zh: 陛下念亦及此乎？

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty's thought extend to this as well?
translations.idiomatic: Does Your Majesty give this any thought at all?

sentences.zh: 王安石輕用己私，紛更法令，棄誠而懷詐，興利而忘義，尚功而悖道，人皆知安石廢祖宗法令，不知其並與祖宗之道廢之也。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi lightly indulged private motives, confusedly changed laws and statutes, abandoned sincerity and harbored deceit, promoted profit and forgot righteousness, valued achievement and violated the Way. People all know Anshi abolished the ancestral laws and statutes, but do not know he abolished the ancestral Way together with them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi acted on private impulse, churning through laws and codes; he cast off sincerity for cunning, prized profit over righteousness, exalted achievement against the Way. All know Anshi scrapped the ancestral statutes — few see that he scrapped the ancestral Way with them.

sentences.zh: 邪說既行，正論屏棄，故奸諛敢挾紹述之義以逞其私，下誣君父，上欺祖宗，誣謗宣仁，廢遷隆祐。

translations.literal: Once heterodox doctrine prevailed, upright discourse was cast aside; hence treacherous flatterers dared wield the doctrine of 'continuing the legacy' to pursue private ends — below defaming lord and father, above deceiving the ancestors, slandering Xuanren, deposing and relocating Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: When deviant teaching took hold, honest debate was silenced; flatterers then wrapped themselves in 'continuation of the founder's work' to serve private ends — defaming the living ruler and deceased father below, deceiving the ancestors above, reviling Empress Dowager Xuanren and deposing Empress Dowager Longyou.

sentences.zh: 使我國家君臣父子之間，頓生疵癘，三綱廢壞，神化之道泯然將滅。

translations.literal: It made between ruler and minister, father and son in our state suddenly arise plague-spots; the Three Bonds were broken, and the Way of divine transformation nearly extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Between ruler and minister, father and son, our realm suddenly broke out in moral blight; the Three Bonds crumbled, and the Way of transforming governance all but died.

sentences.zh: 遂使敵國外橫，盜賊內訌，王師傷敗，中原陷沒，二聖遠棲於沙漠，皇輿僻寄於東吳，囂囂萬姓，未知攸底，禍至酷也。

translations.literal: Thus the enemy state rampaged abroad, bandits rebelled within, the imperial armies were wounded and defeated, the Central Plain fell, the Two Sages dwelt far in the desert, the imperial carriage lodged obscurely in Eastern Wu, and the clamorous myriad people knew not where it would end — calamity reached the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy power roared without; bandits rose within; imperial armies were broken; the Central Plain was lost; the Two Emperors languished in the desert; the throne was a fugitive in the southeast; a clamoring multitude saw no end — calamity at its cruelest.

sentences.zh: 若猶習於因循，憚於更變，亡三綱之本性，昧神化之良能，上以利勢誘下，下以智術干上。

translations.literal: If still accustomed to routine and afraid of change, losing the original nature of the Three Bonds and obscuring the fine capacity of divine transformation — above using profit and power to entice below, below using clever schemes to importune above.
translations.idiomatic: If you still cling to inertia and fear reform, void the Three Bonds of their true nature and blind Heaven's transforming power — the court baiting subjects with gain and rank, subjects importuning the court with schemes.

sentences.zh: 是非由此不公，名實由此不核，賞罰由此失當，亂臣賊子由此得志，人紀由此不修，天下萬事倒行逆施，人欲肆而天理滅矣。

translations.literal: Right and wrong thereby become unjust, name and reality thereby unverified, rewards and punishments thereby improper, treacherous ministers and wicked sons thereby attain their aims, human order thereby unregulated, all affairs under Heaven run backward and in reverse — human desires run wild and Heavenly principle is extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Then right and wrong lose fairness, names and facts go unreconciled, rewards and punishments miss their mark, traitors prosper, human order rots, all under Heaven runs backward — desire unchecked and Heavenly principle quenched.

sentences.zh: 將何以異於先朝，求救禍亂而致昇平乎？

translations.literal: How then will this differ from the former court, or rescue you from chaos and disorder to reach lofty peace?
translations.idiomatic: How will this differ from the last reign? How can it save us from chaos and restore peace?

sentences.zh: 末言：

translations.literal: Closing remarks:
translations.idiomatic: In closing:

sentences.zh: 高閌為國子司業，請幸太學，宏見其表，作書責之曰：

translations.literal: Gao Kan was Vice Director of the Directorate of Education; he petitioned for an imperial visit to the Imperial Academy. Hong saw his memorial and wrote a letter reproving him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kan, Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, petitioned for an imperial visit to the Imperial Academy. Hong read his memorial and wrote to rebuke him, saying:

sentences.zh: 太學，明人倫之所在也。

translations.literal: The Imperial Academy is where human relations are made clear.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Academy exists to clarify human relations.

sentences.zh: 昔楚懷王不返，楚人憐之，如悲親戚。

translations.literal: Formerly, when King Huai of Chu did not return, the people of Chu pitied him as if mourning kin.
translations.idiomatic: When King Huai of Chu never came home, the people of Chu mourned him like a kinsman lost.

sentences.zh: 蓋忿秦之以強力詐其君，使不得其死，其憯勝於加之以刃也。

translations.literal: For they resented that Qin by force and fraud held their lord, not allowing him to die as he ought — a cruelty worse than putting blade to him.
translations.idiomatic: They hated Qin for using force and deceit to hold their king and deny him a proper death — worse than killing him outright.

sentences.zh: 太上皇帝劫制於強敵，生往死歸，此臣子痛心切骨，臥薪嘗膽，宜思所以必報也。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor was seized and held by a powerful enemy; alive he went forth, dead he returned — this cuts ministers and sons to the bone. Sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall, one ought to think how this must surely be avenged.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor was hostage to a mighty foe — he went alive and came back dead. Every loyal subject should feel it in his bones, sleep on brushwood and taste gall, and brood on vengeance that cannot be refused.

sentences.zh: 而柄臣乃敢欺天罔人，以大仇為大恩乎？

translations.literal: Yet the power-holding minister dares deceive Heaven and delude men, treating the greatest feud as the greatest grace?
translations.idiomatic: And the power-holding minister dares deceive Heaven and mankind, calling the greatest feud the greatest grace?

sentences.zh: 昔宋公為楚所執，及楚子釋之，孔子筆削《春秋》，乃曰：「許侯盟於薄，釋宋公。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Song was seized by Chu; when the ruler of Chu released him, Confucius edited the Spring and Autumn Annals and wrote: "The Marquis of Xu allied at Bo, releasing Duke Song of Song."
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Song of Song was taken by Chu and later released, Confucius edited the Spring and Autumn Annals to record: "The Marquis of Xu allied at Bo, releasing Duke Song."

sentences.zh: 」不許楚人制中國之命也。

translations.literal: " — he would not permit the men of Chu to control the fate of the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: " — refusing to let Chu dictate the destiny of the Central States.

sentences.zh: 太母，天下之母，其縱釋乃在金人，此中華之大辱，臣子所不忍言也。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress, mother of the realm — that her release came at the hands of the Jurchens is the greatest humiliation of China, what ministers and sons cannot bear to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress was mother of the realm; that her release owed to the Jurchens is China's deepest shame — what loyal subjects cannot bear to utter.

sentences.zh: 而柄臣乃敢欺天罔人，以大辱為大恩乎？

translations.literal: Yet the power-holding minister dares deceive Heaven and delude men, treating the greatest humiliation as the greatest grace?
translations.idiomatic: Yet that minister dares still deceive Heaven and men, calling the deepest shame the highest favor?

sentences.zh: 晉朝廢太后，董養遊太學，升堂歎曰：「天下之理既滅，大亂將作矣。

translations.literal: When the Jin dynasty deposed the Empress Dowager, Dong Yang visited the Imperial Academy, ascended the hall and sighed: "The principle of the realm is already extinguished; great disorder will soon arise."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin deposed their empress dowager, Dong Yang entered the Imperial Academy, mounted the hall, and sighed: "The moral order of the realm is dead; great disorder is near."

sentences.zh: 」則引遠而去。

translations.literal: " — then he withdrew far and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " — then he withdrew and left.

sentences.zh: 今閣下自睹忘仇滅理，北面敵國，以苟宴安之事，猶偃然為天下師儒之首。

translations.literal: Now you, sir, yourself witness forgetting the feud and extinguishing principle, facing north toward the enemy state for temporary feasting and ease — yet you complacently stand as chief teacher of the realm's scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Today you see the feud forgotten and moral order extinguished, bowing north to the enemy for a little feasting and ease — and still you sit at ease as chief teacher of the empire.

sentences.zh: 既不能建大論，明天人之理以正君心；

translations.literal: Unable even to establish great doctrine, clarifying the principle of Heaven and man to rectify the ruler's heart;
translations.idiomatic: You cannot even raise great doctrine, show Heaven-and-man's principle, and set the ruler's heart straight;

sentences.zh: 乃阿諛柄臣，希合風旨，求舉太平之典，又為之詞云云，欺天罔人孰甚焉！

translations.literal: instead you flatter the power-holding minister, hoping to match prevailing intent, seek to hold ceremonies of great peace, and moreover compose words and phrases for it — who deceives Heaven and deludes men more than this!
translations.idiomatic: instead you fawn on the power-holder, bend to his will, plead for rites of 'great peace,' and dress it in fine phrases — who deceives Heaven and men more thoroughly than this!

sentences.zh: 宏初以蔭補右承務郎，不調。

translations.literal: Hong at first received appointment as Right Assistant Director for Works by inherited privilege; he never took up a post.
translations.idiomatic: Hong first received an appointment as Right Assistant Director for Works through inherited privilege and never reported for duty.

sentences.zh: 秦檜當國，貽書其兄寅，問二弟何不通書，意欲用之。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui held power, he sent a letter to Hong's elder brother Yin, asking why the two younger brothers did not write letters — intending to employ them.
translations.idiomatic: While Qin Hui dominated the court, he wrote to Hong's elder brother Yin asking why the two younger brothers never wrote; he meant to bring them into service.

sentences.zh: 寧作書止敘契好而已。

translations.literal: Ning wrote a letter that only narrated old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Ning replied with a letter that spoke only of their old friendship.

sentences.zh: 宏書辭甚厲，人問之，宏曰：「政恐其召，故示之以不可召之端。

translations.literal: Hong's letter language was very stern. When people asked him, Hong said: "I am just afraid he may summon me, so I show signs that I cannot be summoned."
translations.idiomatic: Hong's letter was fierce in tone. When asked about it, he said: "I feared he might summon me, so I gave him reason to think me unsummonable."

sentences.zh: 」檜死，宏被召，竟以疾辭，卒於家。

translations.literal: " When Hui died, Hong was summoned; he declined on grounds of illness and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: " When Hui died, Hong was summoned; he pleaded illness, declined, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 著書曰《知言》。

translations.literal: He authored a book titled Knowing Words.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a work titled Knowing Words.

sentences.zh: 張栻謂其言約義精，道學之樞要，制治之蓍龜也。

translations.literal: Zhang Shi called its words concise and meaning precise — the hinge of the learning of the Way, the divining tortoise for ordering governance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi praised it as concise in speech and precise in meaning — the pivot of Dao learning, the oracle for governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 有詩文五卷、《皇王大紀》八十卷。

translations.literal: He left five fascicles of poetry and prose, and eighty fascicles of Great Chronicle of Emperors and Kings.
translations.idiomatic: His literary remains include five fascicles of poetry and prose and eighty fascicles of Great Chronicle of Emperors and Kings.

translations.literal: 〈Sons〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Sons〉

sentences.zh: 寧

translations.literal: Ning
translations.idiomatic: Ning

sentences.zh: 寧字和仲，以蔭補官。

translations.literal: Ning, styled Hezhong, received office by inherited privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Ning, courtesy name Hezhong, entered office through inherited privilege.

sentences.zh: 秦檜當國，召試館職，除敕令所刪定官。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui held power, he was summoned for examination for a post in the Academy and appointed Editor at the Edict Drafting Office.
translations.idiomatic: While Qin Hui held power, Ning was summoned for an Academy post examination and appointed as editor at the Edict Drafting Office.

sentences.zh: 秦熺知樞密院事，檜問寧曰：「熺近除，外議云何？

translations.literal: Qin Xi became Director of the Privy Bureau; Hui asked Ning: "Xi was recently appointed — what does outside opinion say?"
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Xi was made Director of the Privy Bureau, Hui asked Ning: "Xi has just been appointed — what do people outside the court say?"

sentences.zh: 」寧曰：「外議以為相公必不為蔡京之所為也。

translations.literal: " Ning said: "Outside opinion holds that the Chancellor surely will not do what Cai Jing did."
translations.idiomatic: " Ning answered: "Outside opinion holds that the Chancellor surely will not repeat what Cai Jing did."

sentences.zh: 」遷太常丞、祠部郎官。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Secretariat Gentleman in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then promoted to Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Secretariat Gentleman in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 初，以寧父兄故召用，及寅與檜忤，乃出寧為夔路安撫司參議官。

translations.literal: At first he was summoned and employed because of Ning's father and elder brothers; when Yin fell out with Hui, Ning was sent out as Adviser on the Pacification Commission of the Kuizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He had first been called to office because of his father and elder brothers; once Yin broke with Hui, Ning was posted as adviser on the Kuizhou Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 除知澧州，不赴。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Lizhou but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Lizhou but refused to go.

sentences.zh: 主管台州崇道觀，卒。

translations.literal: He served as Superintendent of the Chongdao Abbey in Taizhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the Chongdao Abbey in Taizhou and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 安國之傳《春秋》也，修纂檢討盡出寧手。

translations.literal: When Anguo transmitted the Spring and Autumn Annals, the compilation, collation, and review all came from Ning's hand.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Anguo worked on the Spring and Autumn, the compilation and editorial review were largely Ning's work.

sentences.zh: 寧又著《春秋通旨》，以羽翼其書云。

translations.literal: Ning also authored General Purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals to complement that book.
translations.idiomatic: Ning also wrote General Purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals to support his father's book.
